title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Shared radix-4 combinational divider for RV32M
motivation:
The baseline achieves 12.12 CoreMark iterations/second at a median Fmax
of 5.442 MHz. Its reported worst path is 199.837 ns through 156 cells,
including forwarding and u_ex/u_alu. The four signed/unsigned division
and remainder expressions in alu.sv are the strongest candidate for
this unusually deep arithmetic path, although the module-level report
does not identify the exact arithmetic operator. Even infrequent DIV
instructions constrain the clock of every CoreMark instruction. There
are no earlier divider experiments or recorded lessons in this fixture.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU combinational datapath with one
explicitly shared, unsigned-magnitude radix-4 restoring divider that
produces quotient and remainder together. Keep the ALU interface and
all pipeline, forwarding, retirement, and bus-stall behavior unchanged.
This is a local arithmetic implementation optimization with no added
registers, cycles, or handshake signals.

For signed operations, form 32-bit unsigned operand magnitudes, retaining
0x80000000 as the magnitude of INT_MIN. Zero-extend the divisor to 34 bits
and precompute D, 2D, and 3D once. Unroll exactly 16 quotient-digit steps,
consuming the dividend two bits at a time from most significant to least
significant. Start with remainder R=0. At each step form the 34-bit trial
value T={R[31:0], next_two_dividend_bits}. Compute T-D, T-2D, and T-3D in
parallel as explicitly unsigned 35-bit subtractions. The top subtraction
bit indicates underflow; use it directly instead of placing a separate
comparison before subtraction. Select the largest non-underflowing
multiple, append its two-bit digit to the quotient, and carry its
difference as the next remainder; select digit zero and T if all three
underflow. For nonzero D, the selected remainder is less than D and fits
in 32 bits. Express digit selection with mutually exclusive enables so
synthesis can use a parallel selection network. Keep intermediate widths
explicit and permit constant propagation of leading zero dividend bits.

Apply quotient negation for signed operands with opposite signs and
remainder negation only when the original dividend was negative. Handle
division by zero explicitly: quotient all ones and remainder the original
dividend. Preserve INT_MIN/-1 quotient INT_MIN and remainder zero. Leave
the RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas exactly unchanged, and leave multiplication
and all RV32I operations unchanged. The real division cone should contain
no /, %, or quotient-times-divisor reconstruction multiplier.

The expected benefit is fewer serial quotient-digit steps, from a typical
radix-2 implementation's 32 to 16, plus shared quotient/remainder hardware.
CoreMark cycles should remain identical for the same stall sequence, so
any Fmax improvement translates directly into fitness. The estimate is
unmeasured: three parallel subtractors per digit, divisor fanout, and
selection routing could offset the depth reduction. Judge the result with
the existing Gowin median-Fmax flow and CoreMark CRC/cosimulation gates;
the required acceptance threshold is fitness above 12.67752. Keep every
existing correctness check, including ordinary ALTOPS formal, and validate
the real arithmetic with ALU tests and non-ALTOPS formal-deep when feasible.

title: Replace the combinational divider with a bounded iterative execution unit
motivation:
The only recorded experiment is the baseline: fitness 12.12, median Fmax
5.442 MHz, 12,312 LUT4s, and a 199.837 ns, 156-cell critical path through
forwarding and u_ex/u_alu. There are no prior structural attempts and no
LESSONS.md. The ALU currently synthesizes signed and unsigned division and
remainder as combinational / and % operators. These are the strongest
suspected source of the very deep execute path; they constrain every
instruction's clock period even when no division executes. Moving this
arithmetic into a registered, shared unit should substantially improve
frequency and area at the cost of extra cycles only for DIV/REM operations.

remainder as combinational / and % operators. These are the strongest

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU blocking multicycle EX operations using one
shared unsigned restoring divider that generates four quotient bits per
cycle. Keep the existing single-issue pipeline, combinational RV32I ALU,
and multiplier. Remove real combinational / and % from the synthesized
core. This is one structural change: decouple long division from ordinary
single-cycle execution, without adding a cache, predictor, or wider issue.

Capture the fully forwarded operands, operation, signedness, and RVFI
metadata exactly once when a valid division is accepted. Normalize signed
operands at launch. Use eight iterations of four explicitly unrolled
restoring steps, each with a 33-bit trial remainder/subtraction, a quotient
shift register, and a registered divisor. Select quotient or remainder and
apply the appropriate sign on the final iteration, transferring directly
into EX/MEM without an extra completion cycle. Budget at most nine EX
occupancy cycles including operand capture. This bound is deliberate:
with ready buses, even a taken branch or load-use bubble immediately before
a division must leave at most ten cycles between retirements, satisfying
the unchanged liveness 1 10 20 check. Confirm this bound with directed
sequences and formal; do not solve a failure by changing formal depths or
shortening only the formal model's execution latency.

Hold fetch and ID/EX while a division occupies EX. Distinguish this hold
from a data-memory stall: older EX/MEM and MEM/WB instructions must drain
once, and EX/MEM must receive a side-effect-free invalid bubble after an
older instruction advances while the divider is busy. A blocked memory
request must instead retain its payload and current bus-handshake behavior.
Launch only when the downstream memory stage can advance. Captured divider
operands must survive disappearance of forwarding sources as older stages
drain. Publish one completed result through the ordinary EX/MEM forwarding
and WB paths, with exactly one retirement and no repeated launch. If a
completed result cannot advance, retain it until accepted. Gate redirects
and all side effects by valid stage contents and advancement as appropriate.

Preserve RV32M divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 results, truncation toward zero,
and the dividend's sign for nonzero remainders. Compute quotient and remainder
together; no second divider is needed. Preserve all existing ALTOPS formulas
and route their substituted values through the same start/busy/completion
protocol and latency as real division. Keep real and ALTOPS arithmetic tests,
decoder legality, reset cancellation, memory stalls, and channel-0 RVFI
ordering intact. Keep core.yaml nret=1 and the external interface unchanged.

Validate exact arithmetic and pipeline behavior, then run the unmodified
formal suite and CoreMark cosim with both bus stalls, checking all CRCs and
timing markers. Measure median Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle;
accept only if this fitness exceeds 12.67752 (the 4.6 percent threshold).
The main risks are the delay of four cascaded subtract/select steps plus
final sign correction, a multiplier or register-file path becoming the
next frequency limit, and a higher-than-expected dynamic division count.
The expected gain below is a conservative hypothesis, not a measured result.

title: Small bimodal predictor with immediate direct targets
motivation:
The baseline always fetches PC+4 and discards the current fetch whenever EX
resolves a taken conditional branch or jump. Although described as five
stages, IF/ID is combinational, so each such redirect costs one instruction
slot before bus stalls. CoreMark's repeated loops and direct calls offer an
opportunity to recover these slots. There are no previous predictor attempts
in the experiment log and no LESSONS.md. The measured critical path runs
through forwarding and the combinational ALU; this proposal targets cycles
per iteration and does not claim to fix that arithmetic timing bottleneck.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one fetch-time direct-control-flow predictor: a 128-entry, two-bit
saturating bimodal direction table indexed by PC[8:2], plus exact immediate
targets for legal conditional branches and JAL. Reset counters to weakly
taken (2'b10). Predict an aligned legal branch taken when its counter MSB
is set, and predict an aligned JAL unconditionally. Compute B/J immediates
from the raw imem_data and add them to the current fetch PC. All other
instructions, including JALR and reserved branch encodings, predict PC+4.
Use no BTB, global history, return stack, or additional pipeline stage.

Carry one predicted_taken bit with the accepted instruction into ID/EX.
This is sufficient because every predicted target is the instruction's
exact PC-relative target, and indirect jumps are never predicted. EX keeps
the existing forwarded-operand comparisons, target calculation, alignment
traps, and RVFI pc_next semantics. Define actual_taken as a taken branch or
jump with no target-alignment fault. Recover only when a valid, advancing
EX instruction has actual_taken != predicted_taken. Recover to the resolved
target when actually taken, otherwise to that instruction's PC+4. Correctly
predicted branches and JAL must neither flush nor insert a bubble; aligned
JALR still redirects in EX, and a misaligned transfer still traps exactly
as in the baseline. Avoid a new 32-bit predicted-target comparison.

Prediction advances the PC only when the current fetch is actually accepted
into ID/EX: imemReady, no load-use stall, no dmem stall, and no recovery.
Latch prediction metadata with exactly the same enables as the instruction;
bubbles clear it and a held ID/EX entry retains it. Recovery has priority
over an imem stall or a younger load-use condition. During an older dmem
stall, defer both recovery and predictor training until EX can advance;
keep the unresolved instruction and its metadata intact. Thus a held branch
cannot repeatedly redirect, accidentally squash its correct successor, or
train multiple times. Retain the existing MEM/WB forwarding preservation.

Train once per valid, legal, non-faulting conditional branch advancing out
of EX, using its own PC index and resolved direction. Increment or decrement
the current indexed counter with saturation, not a counter snapshot saved
at fetch. Do not train on JAL, JALR, bubbles, squashed instructions, or held
instructions. A same-index lookup and update may observe the pre-edge
counter; correctness depends on the saved prediction bit, never a reread
of the table in EX. Reset only predictor state in addition to existing
reset behavior. Keep the single-channel nret=1 interface, decoder legality,
M-extension arithmetic, memory handshake, and all evaluation checks intact.

The expected gain is roughly 8 percent in end-to-end fitness, principally
from fewer redirect bubbles at approximately unchanged Fmax. This is a
prediction, not a measured result. The main risks are branch-table aliasing,
nearly unbiased branch outcomes, and added fetch mux routing. Validate
stall/recovery interactions and unchanged architectural execution before
measuring canonical CoreMark cycles and median Gowin Fmax. Acceptance still
requires fitness above 12.67752, more than 4.6 percent above 12.12.

title: Two parallel radix-4 digits per iterative divider cycle
motivation:
The champion reaches 84.60 CoreMark iterations/second at 37.999 MHz.
Its reported worst path starts at u_ex/u_div/remainder_q and passes
through the divider and execute stage, with 30.772 ns arrival and 138
cells. The divider computes four quotient bits per iteration using
four serial 33-bit subtract/select steps, followed on completion by
result selection and sign correction. This remaining arithmetic depth
constrains the clock of every instruction. The previous micro_opt
attempt, hyp-20261001-001-r1s0, used a fully combinational radix-4
divider and reached only 5.936 MHz because sixteen digit steps still
lay in one cycle. The successful iterative design supplies the missing
register boundaries; optimize the arithmetic inside those boundaries.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion reaches 84.60 CoreMark iterations/second at 37.999 MHz.
Its reported worst path starts at u_ex/u_div/remainder_q and passes
through the divider and execute stage, with 30.772 ns arrival and 138
cells. The divider computes four quotient bits per iteration using
four serial 33-bit subtract/select steps, followed on completion by
result selection and sign correction. This remaining arithmetic depth
constrains the clock of every instruction. The previous micro_opt
attempt, hyp-20261001-001-r1s0, used a fully combinational radix-4
divider and reached only 5.936 MHz because sixteen digit steps still
lay in one cycle. The successful iterative design supplies the missing
register boundaries; optimize the arithmetic inside those boundaries.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real arithmetic recurrence inside div_unit.sv with
two cascaded radix-4 restoring digit steps per existing iteration.
Each step chooses among three parallel trial subtractions, halving
the number of serial subtract/select stages from four to two while
still producing four quotient bits per cycle. This is a local divider
datapath optimization. Preserve its interface, launch conditions,
eight iterations, nine-cycle EX occupancy including capture, final-edge
acceptance, and held-completion behavior. Preserve the pipeline and
all instruction and data memory stall behavior.

At the existing operand-capture edge, normalize signed operands as
today, latch the 32-bit unsigned divisor magnitude D, and additionally
latch the exact 34-bit value 3D, formed by widened addition of D and
D shifted left once. Form D and 2D as zero-extended wiring from the
captured divisor. Do not recompute 3D from the changing remainder or
place its adder inside either iterative digit step. Keep the dividend
in the existing quotient shift register and start the remainder at zero.

For each of two digit steps, construct the unsigned 34-bit trial value
T={R[31:0], Q[31:30]}. Compute {1'b0,T}-{1'b0,D},
{1'b0,T}-{1'b0,2D}, and {1'b0,T}-{1'b0,3D} in parallel as explicitly
35-bit unsigned subtractions; all three multiples here are 34 bits.
Bit 34 of each difference identifies underflow. Choose the largest
multiple without underflow, or digit zero and T if all underflow.
Express the four choices with mutually exclusive enables and a
parallel masked-OR data selection, avoiding a serial priority data
mux and any separate compare-then-subtract path. Append the chosen
two-bit digit to Q[29:0] and carry the selected remainder into the
next digit step. For nonzero D, R<D ensures the selected remainder
fits 32 bits; keep the trial and multiples widened until selection.
Register Q and R after both digit steps exactly where the current
four restoring steps register their outputs.

Preserve final quotient/remainder selection and signed correction,
including truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainder, the
INT_MIN/-1 result, and divide-by-zero quotient 0xffffffff with the
original dividend as remainder. With D=0 the largest digit is three
at every step and subtraction leaves the dividend prefix unchanged;
retain the existing quotient override to suppress incorrect sign
correction. Preserve reset cancellation, ignored starts while busy,
result retention under accept=0, and exactly one acceptance. Leave
the RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas and their identical real/ALTOPS
scheduling untouched. No new cycle, early-out, or formal-only shortcut
is part of this proposal.

CoreMark cycle count should remain 4,491,485 for the same workload
and bus-stall sequence, so the benefit should come entirely from
higher median Gowin Fmax. A 20 percent fitness improvement is an
unmeasured estimate, corresponding to roughly 45.60 MHz and 101.52
iterations/second. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 88.4916,
or roughly 39.75 MHz if cycles are unchanged. Principal risks are
routing and divisor fanout from six parallel subtractors, a slower
signed-normalization/3D capture path, final sign correction, and a
different critical path becoming dominant. Area has headroom from
the champion's 2,691 LUT4s, but only vendor timing can establish gain.

A fixed-width Python model of the proposed two-digit recurrence passed
80,000 reference comparisons covering all four DIV/REM operations,
directed boundary operands and seeded random pairs. It also checked
one-hot digit selection and R<D for nonzero divisors at every digit.
This supports arithmetic feasibility; RTL and timing remain unmeasured.

Validate the real divider with exact directed and seeded randomized
arithmetic tests, plus its unchanged latency/backpressure tests in
both real and ALTOPS builds. Run the existing pipeline dependency,
stall, reset, retirement-bound tests and the unchanged formal suite.
Use CoreMark cosimulation with both bus stalls, canonical CRCs and
timing markers, then the normal median Gowin Fmax fitness evaluation.
Preserve all correctness gates, nret=1, and the exact top-level IO.

title: Retime divider completion using first-nibble work during operand capture
motivation:
The champion achieves fitness 84.60 at 37.999 MHz. Its reported worst
path starts at u_ex/u_div/remainder_q and spans 30.772 ns and 138 cells.
The successful structural attempt hyp-20261001-002-r1s1 removed full
combinational division, but the last iteration still cascades four
full-width restoring subtract/select steps with 32-bit sign correction
and EX result selection. This completion path is a strong candidate
for the remaining divider timing limit. The recorded CoreMark cycle
count is 4,491,485 for both the original baseline and this champion,
making frequency the clearest measured opportunity in this workload.

LESSONS.md confirms the benefit of bounded iterative division. The
earlier micro_opt hyp-20261001-001-r1s0 left all 16 radix-4 digit stages
combinational and reached only 5.936 MHz. This proposal instead moves
arithmetic across the existing divider register boundary. Simply adding
a completion cycle risks the unchanged ten-cycle retirement-gap check;
doing inexpensive first-nibble work at capture makes room for a separate
sign-correction phase without extending the nine-cycle EX occupancy.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition blocking DIV/REM into three phases: operand capture with
first-nibble division, seven registered four-bit restoring iterations,
and a final sign-correction/transfer phase. Keep the existing start,
busy, done, accept interface and exact nine-cycle instruction schedule.
The single architectural change is divider stage retiming: the full
unsigned quotient and remainder must be registered before sign
correction, with the cycle recovered by moving the first four quotient
bits into launch. Retain the existing four-binary-step recurrence for
all remaining digits.

On an accepted launch, compute the same 32-bit unsigned magnitudes A
and D as today, preserving INT_MIN as 0x80000000. The first dividend
nibble N=A[31:28] is at most 15. If any D[31:4] bit is set, its quotient
nibble is necessarily zero and its remainder is N. Otherwise compute
the four-bit quotient q4 and remainder r4 of N divided by D[3:0] using
four explicitly small restoring steps starting with zero remainder.
These steps need only four-bit trial values and five-bit unsigned
subtract/borrow results; their intermediate trial values cannot exceed
the already consumed prefix of N. Use explicit narrow widths rather
than a full-width divider or synthesis of / and %. With D=0 this same
small restoring network yields q4=15 and r4=N, matching the existing
divide-by-zero recurrence.

At the existing capture edge, initialize quotient_q={A[27:0],q4},
remainder_q={28'b0,r4}, and divisor_q=D. Capture signs, operation and
zero-divisor status exactly as before. For seven subsequent edges,
process four more dividend bits per cycle with the existing 33-bit
trial/subtract and 32-bit quotient/remainder registers. Four launch
bits plus seven times four recurrence bits complete the full 32-bit
division. In the next cycle, select quotient_q or remainder_q directly,
correct its sign, apply the zero-divisor quotient override, and present
done/result for EX/MEM acceptance. No combinational recurrence output
may feed this final sign-correction phase.

Preserve the existing iteration counter's externally visible timing:
accepted capture initializes iteration_q=0; seven recurrence edges
advance it to 7; done asserts with iteration_q=7 and EX/MEM accepts at
the next edge, exactly when the old eighth iteration completed. Freeze
the unsigned quotient/remainder when iteration_q=7. If accept is low,
latch the corrected result in the existing result_q, set complete_q,
and hold until acceptance. Reset must cancel every phase. Only an
accepted start may sample operands; forwarding changes while busy
must have no effect.

Keep real and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS scheduling identical, including all
exceptional inputs. Preserve all ALTOPS formulas and the existing EX
metadata capture, downstream draining, bus-stall behavior, forwarding,
decoder legality and channel-0 retirement. Preserve RV32M truncation
toward zero, dividend-signed remainder, INT_MIN/-1, quotient all ones
on division by zero, and the original dividend as zero-divisor remainder.
Leave nret=1, top-level ports and every correctness check unchanged.

The new longest divider paths should be either four restoring steps
into the quotient/remainder registers or registered magnitude through
sign correction and result selection. The old completion path composed
both. The launch path gains only a narrow nibble divider after magnitude
normalization, plus a reduction test for large divisors. No extra
execution cycles or CoreMark IPC penalty are intended. This proposal
changes the execution schedule inside the unit, without requiring a
new frontend policy, speculation, wider issue or memory optimization.

Validate the real arithmetic and the unchanged nine-cycle handshake
with existing tests plus exhaustive small-divider initialization cases,
all dividend top nibbles, high-bit operands, sign-conversion carry cases,
and deterministic full-width differential vectors. Run the existing
pipeline tests, unmodified formal gate and CoreMark cosim with both bus
stalls, canonical CRCs, validation text and MMIO timing brackets. Check
identical retirement timing for fixed inputs and stall sequences and
retain the ready-bus maximum ten-cycle retirement-gap assertion. Real
arithmetic tests are essential because default formal uses ALTOPS.

During hypothesis preparation, a standalone bit-accurate model of the
narrow initialization and seven remaining iterations passed 85,284
comparisons against independent RV32M arithmetic, including all four
operations, small divisors, top-nibble boundaries and signed edge cases.
This supports the arithmetic decomposition; RTL, handshake and timing
validation still belong to implementation.

Measure median vendor Fmax times measured CoreMark iterations/cycle.
Acceptance requires fitness greater than 88.4916, or approximately
39.746 MHz if cycles remain 4,491,485. The forecast is an unmeasured
15 percent fitness improvement. Main risks are four-step recurrence
delay remaining dominant, launch normalization plus nibble initialization
becoming critical, a multiplier or forwarding path limiting Fmax, and
off-by-one errors at the recurrence-to-correction boundary. Inspect
Gowin paths and resource use before attributing any gain to retiming.

title: Recover branch bubbles with a stall-safe bimodal predictor
motivation:
The current champion already has the iterative divider and reaches 84.60
fitness at 37.999 MHz, but still fetches sequentially and flushes on every
taken branch or jump. IF/ID is combinational, so each redirect discards
one instruction slot, rather than the two implied by the stage comments.
The prior predictor experiment hyp-20261001-003-r1s2 passed formal and
cosimulation and reduced measured CoreMark cycles from 4,491,485 to
4,202,246. Its 13.32 fitness and regression label reflect a design still
limited by the old combinational divider; they do not show a cycle-count
regression. The current champion has the same 4,491,485 measured cycles
as the old baseline. Applying the demonstrated predictor to this champion
is therefore a promising isolated predictor change. LESSONS.md also shows
that local counter updates improved Gowin timing versus an indexed
read-modify-write implementation, so use that implementation from the start.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 128-entry, two-bit saturating bimodal direction predictor with exact
immediate targets for conditional branches and JAL to the current RTL.
Keep the current iterative DIV/REM unit, its nine-cycle EX occupancy,
multiplier, forwarding, and pipeline topology. This proposal changes only
prediction and its necessary recovery/metadata integration; no BTB, return
stack, global history, cache, or additional pipeline stage is needed.

Index counters with fetch PC[8:2] and reset to weakly taken (2'b10).
Predecode the raw imem_data: only BRANCH opcode with funct3 in {0,1,4,5,6,7}
and JAL are eligible. Form exact sign-extended B/J immediates and add them
to the fetch PC. Predict an aligned conditional branch taken when the
indexed counter MSB is one; predict an aligned JAL taken unconditionally.
Predict PC+4 for everything else, including JALR, illegal branch encodings,
and misaligned direct targets. Do not derive prediction from the flushed
instruction bundle, which can create a feedback path through hazard logic.

Carry just predicted_taken through IF/ID and ID/EX, captured with the
instruction, retained on hold, and cleared on reset or bubble. Exact
immediate targets make a stored 32-bit predicted target and a target
comparator unnecessary. In EX define actual_taken as a resolved branch
or jump whose target is aligned. Recover only when a valid, advancing EX
instruction has actual_taken != its saved predicted_taken. Recovery goes
to the resolved target when taken and to that instruction's PC+4 otherwise.
A correct prediction must neither flush the successor nor insert a bubble.
JALR remains unpredicted and uses the existing forwarded target calculation.
Preserve misalignment traps, suppression of link writes on traps, and the
resolved architectural pc_next reported through RVFI. Prediction never
substitutes for architectural branch resolution or legality checking.

Fetch advances to its predicted successor only when the current instruction
is accepted into ID/EX: imemReady, no load-use interlock, no older data-memory
stall, no execute_busy, and no recovery. Reset has highest priority, then
recovery, then accepted prediction, then hold. Recovery must override an
instruction-bus stall and squash the younger fetch before it enters EX.
Gate EX recovery and training with in.valid && !stall && !execute_busy &&
!reset. An older blocked memory operation therefore defers branch resolution
effects until advancement, and a held branch cannot train or redirect
repeatedly. Preserve the existing divider frontend hold and completion
release: prediction must not advance while division is busy, and a branch
accepted on the divider completion edge must retain its prediction metadata.
Preserve older-stage draining and MEM/WB data retention for forwarding.

Train once for each valid, legal, non-faulting conditional branch advancing
out of EX, using its own PC[8:2] and actual outcome. Increment/decrement the
current counter with saturation; do not write back a stale fetch snapshot.
Implement each entry's saturating transition locally under a decoded write
enable, as supported by the previous timing lesson. Avoid a second indexed
counter read mux feeding one shared update datapath with wide fanout.
Fetch reads only the selected MSB. A simultaneous lookup and update may use
the pre-edge state: correctness depends on the saved prediction, never an
EX reread. Do not train on jumps, bubbles, held instructions, traps, or
squashed fetches. Instruction stalls must not consume invalid bus data.

Expected fitness improvement is approximately 7 percent, with medium
confidence. Reproducing the prior cycle count at 37.999 MHz would yield
approximately 90.42 iterations/second, about 6.9 percent above 84.60.
These are projections, not measurements of the combined implementation.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 88.4916; at 4,202,246 cycles
that requires median Fmax above approximately 37.19 MHz. Thus only about
a 2.1 percent frequency loss can be tolerated. The main risk is added
predictor read/target/recovery routing becoming a timed critical path or
perturbing divider placement; retain the compact one-bit recovery compare
and local counter updates to limit that risk. Branch aliasing and interaction
with the deterministic bus-stall sequence can also change the cycle benefit.

Validate with directed prediction/recovery tests, the unchanged formal
suite, and canonical CoreMark cosim under both bus stalls. Check all CRCs,
UART validation, bounds, timing markers, single-channel RVFI ordering, and
forward progress. Measure actual bracketed cycles and median Gowin Fmax
together; neither a cycle-only gain nor a timing-only gain establishes
acceptance. Keep nret=1, the external IO contract, decoder defaults,
arithmetic behavior and ALTOPS scheduling, and all evaluation gates intact.

title: Remove redirect feedback from decode payload and operand reads
motivation:
The champion scores 103.54 at median Gowin Fmax 46.505 MHz with
4,491,485 measured CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at
EX/MEM rd, crosses forwarding, execute, IF and hazard logic, and ends
at an ID/EX operand register: 29.031 ns arrival and 50 cells. The prior
micro_opt hyp-20261001-001-r2s0 also exposed this path after improving
divider arithmetic, but reached only 97.11 fitness. LESSONS.md and the
experiment log therefore support targeting this remaining control
path rather than repeating the divider recurrence experiment.

Currently EX redirect replaces the entire fetched instruction with
a NOP before decode, register-file address selection and load-use
comparison. The same redirect also clears every ID/EX payload bit.
This creates a combinational feedback path from forwarded branch
resolution into operand reads and payload capture. The existing valid
bits and EX invalid-bubble handling already provide the mechanism to
discard these instructions without changing their payload values.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make frontend bubble insertion operate on validity, removing redirect
from the combinational instruction and ID/EX payload paths. This is
one local control/datapath factoring optimization: preserve every
pipeline boundary, instruction latency, redirect cycle, load-use
bubble, divider schedule and external bus handshake.

In if_stage, drive out.instr directly from imem_data even when flush
or redirect is asserted. Keep out.pc, out.valid, reset PC and PC update
priorities unchanged. In particular, redirect must still override a
held PC, and a missing instruction response must still produce an
invalid fetch. No wrong-path or unready instruction may become valid.

In id_stage, separate valid-bit update from payload update. Reset
still initializes the entire register deterministically to zero.
Thereafter, payload fields (including decoded controls, instruction,
addresses and operand values) capture whenever !stall and otherwise
hold; flush must not clear, gate or select these fields. For valid
alone, retain reset/flush priority over stall: clear on reset or flush,
capture in.valid when !stall, otherwise hold. Do not recreate a wide
NOP/zero mux in decode or on the register-file read addresses. Inactive
payloads remain ordinary defined bits, never explicit X/don't-care
assignments. The existing ex_stage !in.valid case emits an inert zero
EX/MEM bubble before any stale decoded controls can advance.

In hazard_unit, qualify the raw rs1/rs2 load-use comparison with
imem_ready, preserving the old NOP-masking behavior for an unavailable
fetch. Specifically use imem_ready && id_ex_mem_read && id_ex_rd!=0
&& (id_ex_rd==if_id_rs1 || id_ex_rd==if_id_rs2). Keep the existing
valid-qualified id_ex_mem_read supplied by core.sv. Do not qualify
this comparison or payload enable with if_id.valid or !redirect:
those would reintroduce the redirect-to-stall feedback path. Under
the existing validated decoder a valid EX load cannot simultaneously
be a redirecting branch or jump, so a wrong-path raw instruction
cannot cause a load-use stall during redirect. This exclusivity is
part of the correctness argument and must be checked, not assumed
by weakening formal constraints. Preserve all other hazard equations,
including dmem and execute-busy hold priority and flush suppression
while a live instruction must remain held.

Audit every consumer of ID/EX controls against invalid payloads.
Existing validity gating of load-use detection, division start,
redirect and EX/MEM transfer must remain effective. In particular,
a killed load must not create another load-use bubble, a killed
division must not start or hold EX, and killed stores and illegal
instructions must neither access memory nor retire. Preserve the
retained MEM/WB forwarding data during dmem stalls. Keep decoder
default-illegal behavior, all trap checks, real and ALTOPS arithmetic,
nret=1 and the exact core IO contract unchanged.

With the same instruction and bus-ready sequence, architectural
retirements, memory transactions and their cycle positions should
match the champion. CoreMark cycles should remain 4,491,485; the
intended benefit is entirely median Fmax. The 15 percent forecast is
unmeasured, corresponding to roughly 53.48 MHz and 119.07 fitness.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 108.30284, approximately
48.65 MHz if cycles are unchanged. The reported path arrival includes
the vendor timing context and is not itself the scored clock period.

Run the unchanged correctness gates and focused pipeline regressions
covering redirects using both forwarding sources, taken/not-taken
branches, JAL/JALR, misaligned targets, load-use bubbles, instruction
backpressure, data backpressure and divider holds. Exercise a wrong-
path store, load, DIV/REM and illegal word immediately after redirects,
plus legal and illegal garbage on imem_data while imem_ready=0.
Compare cycle-stamped valid RVFI and accepted memory transactions
against the champion on deterministic stall schedules; ignore payload
fields only on invalid retirements. Check exact retirement order,
no wrong-path side effects and the existing forward-progress bound.
Then run CoreMark with both stalls, canonical CRCs, validation text
and MMIO brackets, followed by the normal median Gowin timing flow.
Inspect whether the forwarding/redirect-to-ID operand path disappears.

Risks are missing an invalid-control consumer, reintroducing redirect
through a supposedly helpful hazard-valid gate, increased switching
of invalid payloads, and another path (divider, multiplier or branch
target calculation) limiting the gain. No timing or RTL equivalence
result is claimed at hypothesis preparation time.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the combined fetch/decode boundary into independently
controlled payload and validity state. Flushes and missing fetches
should create bubbles by changing validity, while decoded instruction
data flows independently of the late EX redirect. This is one
structural change to the pipeline's bubble/kill representation and
register control. Preserve stage count, single-issue retirement,
branch resolution timing, the existing one-slot taken-branch bubble,
load-use timing and divider scheduling. No IPC loss is intended.

In if_stage, drive out.instr directly from imem_data and out.pc from
the PC register, including cycles that are invalid or being killed.
Remove the instruction-to-NOP substitution for both redirect and
instruction-bus stalls. Keep fetch validity separate and keep reset
and redirect priority on PC updates exactly as today: a legal redirect
must update PC even when io_imemReady is low. A failed or misaligned
redirect retains the existing trap and sequential-PC behavior.

In id_stage, separate updates of reg_q.valid from every other ID/EX
field. Reset may still initialize the complete payload. After reset,
payload fields capture decoded raw instruction, immediate, register
addresses and values whenever !stall, independently of flush and
in.valid. If stalled they hold. The valid bit alone follows the
existing reset/flush/hold/capture priority: reset or flush clears it;
otherwise !stall captures in.valid; otherwise it holds. Do not use
redirect, flush, or redirect-qualified in.valid as a payload reset,
zeroing mux or capture enable. Capturing wrong-path data with valid=0
is intentional and must never create an architectural action.

Decouple load-use detection from the instruction-to-NOP mux it formerly
depended on. Compare raw instruction source fields against the valid
load in ID/EX, with rd!=0, qualifying the fetch comparison only with
imem_ready. Retain the existing conservative use of both source fields.
In particular, do not qualify this comparison with a fetch-valid bit
that contains redirect: that would recreate the path through hazard
logic to the payload enable. The data-memory and divider hold signals
remain independent of redirect. A valid EX redirect and an EX load-use
interlock are mutually exclusive in this single-issue pipeline; keep
redirect priority explicit at the PC and validity update boundaries.
A data-memory hold still preserves ID/EX and EX/MEM; a divider hold
still preserves ID/EX while older stages drain. Neither may be turned
into a payload-destructive bubble.

Audit every consumer of the now potentially nonzero invalid ID/EX
payload. Preserve in.valid qualification of division launch, redirect
and the load-use producer. Preserve EX's existing all-zero EX/MEM
bubble when !in.valid, so stale reg_write or memory control bits cannot
propagate as live instructions. Keep existing MEM/WB data retention
during data-memory stalls: forwarding deliberately remains usable
after its valid bit clears. Do not indiscriminately add valid gating
to that retained forwarding source. Preserve captured divider metadata,
all arithmetic and ALTOPS formulas, decoder default-illegal behavior,
misalignment traps, x0, and exactly-once channel-0 retirement. The
nret=1 top-level interface and all correctness gates remain unchanged.

The desired netlist result is that the late forwarding/comparison/
redirect path terminates at PC and validity control, without entering
instruction masking, decoder or register-file selection, or the
ID/EX operand payload's reset/enable/data logic. This does not add a
redirect register or defer branch resolution by a cycle. Merely
removing the NOP mux while leaving whole-payload flush clearing is
incomplete: both dependencies must be removed to test the hypothesis.

Validate with directed wrong-path stores, loads, branches, DIV/REM,
illegal instructions and EBREAK behind taken branches/JAL/JALR;
none may issue a side effect, launch division or retire. Cover both
forwarding sources feeding branch operands and JALR targets. Change
imem_data to active instructions while imemReady=0 to verify validity
isolation. Exercise redirect coincident with instruction stalls,
branches held behind stalled memory operations, load-use plus both
bus stalls, and divider completion followed by a taken branch. Check
exact RVFI PC/order/operand traces, store acceptance counts, reset
behavior and the existing ten-cycle ready-bus retirement-gap bound.
Run existing unit tests, unchanged formal checks, and CoreMark cosim
with both bus stalls, canonical CRCs and the existing timing markers.

Expect the same 4,491,485 CoreMark cycles for the identical bus-stall
sequence. Any difference needs a cycle-trace explanation; no frontend
throughput improvement is assumed. Measure median vendor Fmax and
actual bracketed iterations/cycle. Acceptance requires fitness above
108.30284, approximately 48.65 MHz if cycles stay unchanged. A 15 percent
gain, approximately 119.1 fitness at 53.5 MHz, is an unmeasured forecast.
Main risks are the remaining branch-to-valid path or divider recurrence
becoming limiting, routing variability, and accidental use of stale
invalid controls. Inspect Gowin paths to verify the intended structural
cut; simulation alone cannot establish the frequency benefit.

title: Bimodal prediction with a short validity-only recovery path
motivation:
Both prior predictor attempts passed formal and cosim and reduced bracketed
CoreMark cycles from 4,491,485 to 4,202,246. The round-two predictor scored
92.92 at 39.046 MHz on the older divider; it did not include the completion
retiming now present in the 103.54 champion. This is evidence for a roughly
6.9 percent throughput benefit at constant frequency, not evidence that
prediction has already failed on the current champion. However, the current
worst reported path crosses forwarding, EX branch resolution, IF's
redirect-controlled instruction-to-NOP mux, hazard detection, and ID/EX
payload registers. Straight transplantation risks lengthening this newly
exposed recovery path. Implement the demonstrated predictor with recovery
confined to PC selection and instruction validity so that prediction can
save branch slots without routing late branch resolution through decode.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one direct-control-flow predictor to the current retimed-divider core:
a 128-entry two-bit bimodal direction table and exact immediate targets for
conditional branches and JAL, integrated with a short validity-only squash
path. Keep the existing pipeline depth and nine-cycle DIV/REM scheduling.
This is a predictor proposal; the recovery changes are its timing-aware
integration, not an independent arithmetic or memory optimization.

Index the direction table by fetch PC[8:2], reset counters to weakly taken,
and implement each entry's saturating transition locally under its decoded
update enable. Fetch needs only the selected counter MSB. Avoid a second
indexed counter read mux and shared read-modify-write datapath, following
the prior Gowin timing lesson. Predecode raw imem_data for legal BRANCH
funct3 values {0,1,4,5,6,7} and JAL. Form exact sign-extended B/J targets
from the current PC and immediate. Predict aligned branches from the
counter and aligned JAL taken; all other instructions predict PC+4.
JALR remains resolved in EX. No BTB, return stack, global history, or
new fetch pipeline stage is part of this hypothesis.

Carry one predicted_taken bit with the instruction through IF/ID and
ID/EX. Because every predicted target is exact, EX needs only a one-bit
direction comparison, not a saved target and 32-bit target comparator.
Define actual_taken as a resolved taken branch or jump with no target
alignment fault. For a valid advancing EX instruction, recover exactly
when actual_taken differs from its saved prediction. Select the resolved
target when actually taken, otherwise the instruction's PC+4. Correct
predictions do not flush the successor. Preserve existing misalignment
traps, suppressed link writes on faults, and resolved RVFI pc_next.

Crucially, remove late recovery from the combinational instruction and
source-index paths. IF presents raw imem_data to decode; instruction
validity and ID/EX.valid suppress unavailable or squashed instructions.
Load-use comparison uses raw fetch source indices and the valid EX load,
independently of recovery; do not gate that comparison with an IF valid
signal that itself depends on recovery. Keep recovery as an explicit
final-priority control, rather than masking the instruction into a NOP
and then recalculating hazards from that masked instruction.

Separate the ID/EX valid register's flush handling from payload capture.
Reset still initializes the complete bundle. A load-use bubble or EX
recovery clears valid, while payload registers retain or capture using
the ordinary non-recovery hold/capture enables. Recovery must not clear
every decoded field and operand register through a wide data mux. A
captured wrong-path payload is harmless only when its valid bit is zero:
audit that invalid EX contents cannot launch division, redirect, train
prediction, write registers or memory, forward as a producer, or retire.
Clear or invalidate prediction metadata with its instruction, and never
interpret metadata from an invalid slot. The current EX invalid-to-bubble
behavior and valid-qualified hazards provide the required foundation.

Advance fetch and capture prediction metadata together only on acceptance:
imemReady, no load-use interlock, no older data-memory hold, no divider
execute_busy, and no recovery. PC priority remains reset, then recovery,
then accepted predicted successor, then hold. Recovery overrides an
instruction-bus stall and any younger dependency indication. Older dmem
stalls and divider execution preserve ID/EX including its prediction;
a held EX branch must neither redirect nor train until it can advance.
Preserve MEM/WB forwarding-data retention and older-stage draining.

Train once per valid legal non-faulting conditional branch leaving EX,
gated by !reset, !stall, and !execute_busy. Use that branch's PC index,
resolved outcome, and the current local counter state. Jumps, invalid
slots, faulting transfers, and held instructions do not train. Concurrent
lookup/update may observe the pre-edge state; recovery always compares
the prediction actually saved with the accepted instruction. Retain
exact divider completion acceptance and reset behavior unchanged.

At the prior measured 4,202,246 cycles and the champion's 46.505 MHz,
projected fitness is about 110.67, 6.9 percent above 103.54. Acceptance
requires strictly more than 108.30284, so that cycle count needs median
Gowin Fmax above approximately 45.51 MHz. The recovery restructuring
specifically targets preserving that narrow frequency budget; any extra
timing gain is upside, not an assumed measurement. Main risks are the
raw-instruction-to-predicted-PC target adder becoming critical, table
placement perturbing divider timing, and faulty validity/hold priorities.

Validate directed prediction and squash cases, the unchanged formal
suite, and canonical stalled CoreMark cosim, then score actual median
Gowin Fmax times bracketed iterations/cycle. Check CRCs, UART validation,
bounds, timing markers, exact-once channel-0 retirement and forward
progress. Keep core.yaml nret=1, top-level IO, decoder legality defaults,
arithmetic and ALTOPS behavior, and all evaluation contracts unchanged.

title: Shorten divider launch with direct magnitude prefixes and a nibble lookup
motivation:
The current champion scores 112.81 at 47.405 MHz and 4,202,246 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts in the register file and
ends at u_ex/u_div/remainder_q, traversing ID and EX: 27.145 ns and 26
cells. The launch calculation currently serializes operand forwarding,
full-width signed magnitude conversion, and four small restoring steps.
Completion retiming in hyp-20261001-002-r2s1 removed division arithmetic
from the final sign-correction cycle but moved first-nibble work onto
operand capture. The earlier micro_opt radix-4 recurrence experiment
hyp-20261001-001-r2s0 improved its older parent by 14.79 percent, while
hyp-20261001-001-r3s0 removed recovery from decode; neither shortened
this newly exposed launch cone. Optimize this specific combinational
cone without changing instruction latency or the predictor.

hypothesis.motivation:

CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts in the register file and
ends at u_ex/u_div/remainder_q, traversing ID and EX: 27.145 ns and 26
cells. The launch calculation currently serializes operand forwarding,
full-width signed magnitude conversion, and four small restoring steps.
Completion retiming in hyp-20261001-002-r2s1 removed division arithmetic
from the final sign-correction cycle but moved first-nibble work onto
operand capture. The earlier micro_opt radix-4 recurrence experiment
hyp-20261001-001-r2s0 improved its older parent by 14.79 percent, while

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the divider's first-nibble launch calculation with direct
magnitude-prefix logic and a small exact combinational lookup. Preserve
the existing capture of four quotient bits, seven subsequent four-bit
iterations, and final sign/transfer cycle. This is a local Boolean
implementation optimization inside div_unit.sv, with unchanged register
boundaries, arithmetic state, interface, and nine-cycle EX occupancy.

Let neg_a = signed_op && a[31] and neg_b = signed_op && b[31], where
signed_op is true only for DIV and REM. Compute the four-bit prefix N
of the dividend magnitude directly from the original operand:
  N = neg_a ? (~a[31:28] + (a[27:0] == 0)) modulo 16 : a[31:28].
Use an explicitly four-bit inversion and addition. The lower-28-bit
zero reduction supplies the carry into this nibble; no carry need ripple
through a full 32-bit negation before launch remainder calculation.
Likewise compute the divisor's low magnitude nibble D4 directly:
  D4 = neg_b ? (-b[3:0]) modulo 16 : b[3:0].
Compute the predicate L = (unsigned divisor magnitude >= 16) directly:
  L = neg_b ? ((!(&b[31:4])) || (b[3:0] == 0)) : (|b[31:4]).
For a negative signed divisor, magnitudes below 16 occur exactly for
encodings -1 through -15; -16 must take the large-divisor path. These
prefix and range calculations must not depend on dividend_magnitude
or divisor_magnitude's full-width negation outputs.

Replace the four dependent first_nibble subtract/select stages with
a complete 256-entry constant truth table indexed by {N,D4}, returning
packed {Q4,R4}. For D4!=0, its constants encode floor(N/D4) and N%D4.
For D4==0, encode Q4=15 and R4=N, matching four restoring steps for a
zero divisor. Generate literal constants during implementation, using
ordinary combinational SystemVerilog case/constant logic with all
inputs defined; do not introduce runtime division/modulo operators,
clocked memory, new latency, vendor-only primitives, or initialization
files. The small constant function allows LUT factoring instead of
preserving a serial arithmetic recurrence. When L is true, bypass the
table with Q4=0 and R4=N, since the prefix is at most 15.

At the existing launch edge, retain divisor_q <= full divisor magnitude,
quotient_q <= {dividend_magnitude[27:0], selected_Q4}, and remainder_q
<= {28'b0, selected_R4}. Leave all seven full-width iterations, final
sign correction, divide-by-zero override, sign flags and metadata
unchanged. Preserve INT_MIN/-1, dividend-signed remainder, reset
cancellation, ignored starts while busy, done/accept timing and stable
blocked completion. Preserve the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas
and identical scheduling in both arithmetic builds. No ALU, forwarding,
predictor, hazard, memory, pipeline-depth, nret, or IO change is needed.

CoreMark cycles should remain exactly 4,202,246 with the same stall
sequence. A 10 percent fitness gain is an unmeasured estimate from
removing both the long carry dependency and four serial launch steps;
it corresponds to about 52.15 MHz and 124.09 iterations/second.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 117.99926, approximately
49.59 MHz at unchanged cycles. Main risks are lookup synthesis/routing
overhead, the remaining full-width magnitude capture becoming critical,
and a multiplier or iterative-divider path limiting the clock instead.
Only the vendor's median Fmax evaluation can establish the gain.

During hypothesis preparation, a fixed-width Python model passed all
256 nibble truth-table comparisons against the existing restoring
recurrence, plus 312,338 exact signed/unsigned launch-state comparisons
using boundary operands and 100,000 seeded random operand pairs. It
separately checked the direct prefix, low-nibble and range formulas
against full-width magnitude conversion. This validates the proposed
arithmetic identities, not RTL synthesis, formal proof or timing.

Exhaustively verify all 256 lookup entries, then check direct prefix
and range formulas against full-width unsigned magnitudes across signs,
long carry boundaries and seeded random operands. Retain the existing
independent per-iteration prefix-division assertions: the internal
quotient and remainder states must be unchanged at every edge. Run
exact real-arithmetic divider tests, real/ALTOPS protocol tests, existing
pipeline and formal gates, and canonical stalled CoreMark cosimulation
before the normal Gowin fitness flow. Preserve every correctness gate,
RVFI ordering, CRC, memory bound and timing-marker requirement.

title: Register raw divider operands and recover preparation time with an eight-bit prefix
motivation:
The champion scores 112.81 at 47.405 MHz and 4,202,246 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs from u_rf through u_id
and u_ex into u_div/remainder_q: 27.145 ns and 26 cells. The previous
structural attempt hyp-20261001-002-r3s1 exposed the same endpoint.
The successful hyp-20261001-002-r2s1 separated final sign correction
from the restoring recurrence, but did so by adding first-nibble
arithmetic to operand capture. That now combines operand selection,
signed magnitude conversion, and prefix division before the launch
register. A register boundary before arithmetic directly targets this
observed path. Adding a cycle outright risks the existing ten-cycle
ready-bus retirement-gap check, so the arithmetic must be rescheduled
within the existing nine-cycle EX occupancy.

Repartition the blocking divider into raw operand capture, registered

four-bit recurrence cycles, and final sign correction/transfer. The
single structural change is the divider's internal register placement
and work distribution. Preserve the frontend, prediction, ordinary
ALU and multiplier, external interfaces, and division execution latency.

On start && !busy, capture fully forwarded raw a and b into dedicated
32-bit operand registers, together with operation/sign metadata. Do no
magnitude conversion or restoring arithmetic on the path into these
registers. EX continues to capture the original operands and all RVFI
metadata exactly once using its existing div_start protocol. Hold the
active instruction, drain older stages once, and retain the existing
downstream memory-stall and completion-acceptance behavior.

With the existing iteration counter at zero, prepare solely from the
captured operands. Compute unsigned magnitudes A and D, keeping the
representable magnitude 0x80000000 for INT_MIN. Let N=A[31:24]. When
any bit of D[31:8] is set, D>=256>N and the first quotient byte is zero
with remainder N. Otherwise divide the eight-bit prefix N by D[7:0]
using eight explicitly narrow restoring steps starting at remainder
zero. At step j, shift in N[7-j], subtract the zero-extended eight-bit
divisor with a nine-bit unsigned difference, and select the trial or
difference using its borrow bit. Append !borrow to the quotient byte.
An eight-bit trial suffices: before the last step the consumed prefix
is at most 127, so shifting the lower seven remainder bits is exact.
Keep widths explicit, allow leading-zero simplification of the early
steps, and do not infer / or % operators. D=0 naturally yields quotient
byte 0xff and remainder N; preserve the final zero-divisor override.

At the preparation edge set divisor_q=D, quotient_q={A[23:0],q8},
remainder_q={24'b0,r8}, and capture the signed-result flags and divisor
zero flag from the saved operands. For counter values one through six,
perform the existing four full-width restoring steps per edge. Eight
prepared bits plus six times four bits consume all 32 dividend bits.
With the counter at seven, the complete unsigned quotient/remainder
are registered. Select the requested magnitude, correct its sign,
apply exceptional-result selection, and transfer through the existing
EX/MEM result path. No recurrence output feeds final sign correction.

Retain the precise handshake schedule: launch initializes counter=0;
preparation advances it to 1; six recurrence edges advance it to 7;
done and result are then available for the same acceptance edge as
today. EX occupancy remains nine cycles, including launch and transfer.
Freeze arithmetic at completion. If accept is low, use the existing
result_q/complete_q mechanism to retain the corrected result until
accepted. Reset cancels every phase. Subsequent changes to external
operands, forwarding sources or op must not affect an active request.

Preserve all four RV32M operations, truncation toward zero, the
dividend's sign for remainder, quotient all ones and original dividend
remainder for divisor zero, and INT_MIN/-1 quotient INT_MIN with zero
remainder. Keep the existing ALTOPS formulas and exactly the same
scheduling in both real and ALTOPS builds, including exceptional
inputs. Keep nret=1, channel-0 retirement order, decoder legality,
prediction/recovery behavior and all evaluation invariants unchanged.

The intended timing cut ends operand routing at a plain operand
register. Normalization and prefix arithmetic begin from that register
in the following cycle, removing their cascade with register-file and
forwarding delay. Preparation now contains eight narrow restoring
steps, so its delay must be checked rather than assumed harmless.
Other risks are the unchanged full-width recurrence or combinational
multiplier becoming the next limit, added register/control fanout,
and phase-counter mistakes. Do not combine this with a new predictor,
multiplier pipeline, or a rewrite of the main recurrence.

Validate the first-byte arithmetic independently, then retain and run
the existing real/ALTOPS divider tests, pipeline tests and unmodified
formal suite. Cover all 256 prefix values against all 256 small
divisors, the 255/256 boundary, high-bit and signed carry cases, and
random full-width operands. Check exact existing nine-cycle timing,
reset in every phase, result backpressure, operand changes after
capture, forwarding dependencies, both stalled buses, and exact-once
RVFI retirement with the existing ten-cycle ready-bus gap bound.

During hypothesis preparation, an independent bit-accurate Python
model passed 67,840 prefix cases, including the exhaustive 256x256
small-divisor matrix and large-divisor shortcuts, and 135,748 full
RV32M comparisons against integer division with truncation toward
zero. These checks support the arithmetic decomposition only; RTL
handshake correctness and FPGA timing still require implementation.

Measure actual median Gowin Fmax times bracketed CoreMark iterations
per cycle with canonical CRCs, UART validation, memory bounds and
markers. Unchanged cycles are expected, not measured for this proposal.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 117.99926, corresponding
to approximately 49.5862 MHz at 4,202,246 cycles. The forecast of ten
percent improvement is unmeasured; inspect vendor timing to confirm
that the operand-capture path was cut and preparation did not replace
it with an equally slow path.

title: Compact 64-entry agree predictor with backward/forward branch bias
motivation:
The champion already has exact B/J target prediction and a 128-entry
bimodal direction table. Prior predictor attempts establish the value of
local counter updates and recovery confined to PC selection and validity.
A fresh reference trace of the canonical 2K, ten-iteration CoreMark run
contains 529,588 bracketed conditional branches and only 13,735 JALRs.
Sequential trace replay estimates 54,457 direction misses for the existing
bimodal table. Even eliminating those misses offers little cycle headroom
relative to 4,202,246 measured cycles; a larger history predictor is unlikely
to justify its FPGA cost. Instead, encode agreement with each branch's
backward-taken/forward-not-taken bias, allowing a smaller table to retain
accuracy while reducing predictor storage and selection logic.

An isolated RTL prototype of the exact 64-entry direct-indexed agree design
below measured 4,194,434 stalled, marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles and median
Gowin Fmax 51.374 MHz, versus 4,202,246 cycles and 47.405 MHz for the champion.
Its preliminary fitness is 122.4814 iterations/second, 8.57 percent above
112.81. This supports a frequency-oriented predictor change rather than a
claim that direction accuracy alone can deliver a large speedup.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the existing 128x2 bimodal table with a 64x2 agree predictor,
indexed directly by PC[7:2]. Each entry stores a two-bit saturating counter
for agreement with an instruction-derived static bias, not raw taken
direction. Define bias_taken as the sign of the legal conditional branch's
B immediate: backward predicts taken, forward predicts not taken. Reset all
counters to 2'b10, weakly agree. For an eligible branch, predicted_taken is
(counter[1] == imem_data[31]), still qualified by exact target alignment.
JAL remains unconditionally predicted when aligned; JALR remains resolved
in EX. Keep the existing immediate target adder and legal-branch predecode.
Use precisely 64 entries and direct PC[7:2] indexing; no PC hash, history
table, target cache, return stack, or extra pipeline register is needed.

Retain per-entry local saturating transitions with a decoded update enable:
increment toward 2'b11 on agreement, decrement toward 2'b00 on disagreement.
Fetch reads only the selected counter MSB. Keep training independent of an
indexed counter read and shared read-modify-write datapath. The table uses
128 state bits instead of 256 and a 64:1 direction selection instead of
128:1. Oppositely biased branches can share an entry constructively when
each usually follows its own bias, limiting accuracy loss from downsizing.

In EX, export train_index = in.pc[7:2] and train_agree =
(branch_taken == in.imm[31]). Rename the former train_taken feedback to
reflect its new meaning and narrow its index from seven to six bits in
IF, EX and core wiring. Preserve train_valid exactly: a valid, legal,
non-faulting conditional branch advancing with !stall, !execute_busy and
!reset. Saturate from the current local counter state. Held instructions,
squashed slots, jumps and faulting transfers never train. Simultaneous
lookup/update uses pre-edge state, matching current table semantics.

Carry the actual predicted taken direction, not the agree bit, in the
existing predicted_taken pipeline field. Therefore EX's one-bit comparison
against alignment-qualified actual_taken and its redirect target need no
functional change. Preserve fetch acceptance, reset/redirect/accept/hold
PC priority, metadata retention during dmem and divider holds, and the
validity-only squash path. Late resolution must not control raw instruction
data, load-use source indices, or ID/EX payload capture. No bundle expansion,
extra target comparison, or predictor-state rollback is required.

The prototype used the unchanged vendor timing wrapper, stall generator,
constraints and three placement options. Fmax values were 50.874, 51.374
and 51.374 MHz; option-0 area was 3,277 LUT4s and 739 registers versus
3,412 and 867 for the champion, with unchanged 8 LUT-RAMs, 6 BSRAMs and
6 DSPs. Canonical stalled CoreMark completed with both markers, no OOB,
all five expected CRCs, and the required validation text. This is a real
predictor circuit reduction; the measured gain comes predominantly from
physical timing, whose worst path remains outside the predictor. Do not
assume that fewer predictor bits alone guarantee the frequency improvement.

Prototype measurements are preliminary, not a completed formal gate or an
accepted tournament result. Reproduce them after implementation, run the
unchanged formal suite and architectural cosim, and retain all existing
tests while updating their predictor-specific oracle. Acceptance requires
fitness strictly above 117.99926. At 4,194,434 cycles this needs about
49.494 MHz median Fmax. Forecast 8 percent fitness improvement with medium
confidence; placement sensitivity and bias-dependent aliasing remain the
principal risks. Preserve nret=1, every top-level port, decoder defaults,
trap behavior, RVFI ordering, memory handshakes, arithmetic and ALTOPS
scheduling, and all evaluation contracts.

title: Retimed operand selection at the existing ID/EX boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 122.48 at 51.374 MHz median Fmax and 4,194,434
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior micro_opt experiments shortened divider
arithmetic and removed recovery from frontend payload capture. The last
divider-launch rewrite gained only 2.43 percent, exposing other limits.
A fresh champion option-0 Gowin report reproduces 50.874 MHz: its worst
path starts at the register-file BSRAM output, passes through operand
selection and multiplication, and ends at data memory. A divider-launch
path through the same operand-selection logic is only 0.013 ns shorter.
Improving the common operand-read timing boundary can benefit both.

An isolated prototype of the exact change below reaches median Gowin
Fmax 59.313 MHz, with placement results 56.224, 59.313 and 59.313 MHz.
This supports a local operand-path retiming optimization without changing
instruction latency. Early selection alone reached 53.726 MHz median;
distributed register storage alone reached 51.074 MHz. Their combination
removes both late forwarding comparisons and the slow BSRAM launch from
this one timing cone. It is not a pipeline-depth or prediction change.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the existing ID/EX boundary register complete operand-source
decisions alongside operand data. Use distributed RAM for the small
register-file array so Gowin does not absorb its read boundary into a
BSRAM output. In EX, use the saved mutually exclusive enables to select
original operand sources with parallel masked-OR equations. Keep every
instruction's execution, bus-handshake and retirement cycle unchanged.

In reg_file.sv, retain the existing 32x32 array, synchronous writes,
complete reset-to-zero behavior, asynchronous reads, x0 semantics and
same-cycle write-first bypass. Add the Gowin-supported declaration
attribute (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *) to that array. Do not
replace reset with uninitialized storage or change register-file latency.
The prototype maps the complete core to 40 LUT-RAMs and four BSRAMs,
compared with eight LUT-RAMs and six BSRAMs for the champion. This is a
physical storage implementation change; portable simulation and formal
retain the same register-file behavior.

Compute forwarding decisions for the instruction currently in decode,
using raw imem_data[19:15] and [24:20]. Compare each source with the
destination of the instruction currently in ID/EX, which will occupy
EX/MEM after an accepted decode edge, and with the destination currently
in EX/MEM, which will occupy MEM/WB after that edge. These are prospective
producer tags, not the current-stage tags used by the old EX comparator.

Export next_reg_write from EX as in.valid && ctrl_with_trap.reg_write,
using the existing resolved misalignment suppression. Export the
prospective MEM/WB write flag from MEM as ctrl_with_trap.reg_write,
including memory-alignment suppression. Use these flags to qualify the
two prospective producer matches, always excluding destination x0.
EX/MEM remains the younger producer and has priority over MEM/WB.
For each source encode bit 1 = matching younger producer, bit 2 =
matching older producer AND NOT bit 1, and bit 0 = neither producer.
Exactly one source enable is set for every accepted decode instruction.
Preserve the existing qualification semantics rather than using WB's
valid-gated architectural write enable as a forwarding qualification.

Add two three-bit raw source masks and two four-bit ALU source masks
to id_ex_t. Capture them with the existing !stall payload enable in
id_stage, reset them deterministically, and hold them whenever the
corresponding instruction payload is held. As with the current payload,
flush controls validity and prediction metadata, not these source masks.
Form alu_a_sel = {dec_is_auipc, raw_rs1_mask & {3{!dec_is_auipc}}}
and alu_b_sel = {dec_alu_src, raw_rs2_mask & {3{!dec_alu_src}}}
before the ID/EX edge. The high bit selects PC or immediate; lower bits
retain the raw source ordering. Legal decode and default-illegal behavior
remain unchanged.

In EX, each raw operand is the OR of the three original data sources
masked by its registered raw enables: in.rsN_val, fwd_ex_mem and
fwd_mem_wb. Independently form alu_a and alu_b from those original
sources and PC/immediate using the registered four-bit masks. Avoid
recreating a forwarding mux followed by an ALU-source mux. Keep raw
forwarded operands available for branches, JALR, stores, divider capture
and RVFI even when the ALU selects PC or immediate. Preserve the original
ALU, multiplier, divider arithmetic and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas.

The key scheduling condition is that source masks are only consumed by
the instruction with which they were captured. During dmem holds, ID/EX
and EX/MEM remain fixed and MEM/WB retains forwarding data despite valid
clearing, so the saved choices remain correct. During division, capture
operands and metadata once with the existing div_start; later held masks
need not reselect drained producers because the divider uses its captured
operands. On division completion, the held ID/EX destination becomes the
prospective EX/MEM producer for the newly accepted younger instruction.
Load-use bubbles, redirects, invalid slots and reset must not introduce
stale-mask execution. Trap-suppressed writes must never win a match.
Check these conditions with existing assertions and formal, not new
assumptions that restrict legal instruction or stall streams.

The prototype changes only this operand-read and source-control cone.
Option-0 area is 3,404 LUT4s, 702 registers, 40 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs
and six DSPs, versus 3,277 LUT4s, 739 registers, eight LUT-RAMs, six
BSRAMs and six DSPs for the champion. The timing flow uses the unchanged
FPGA wrapper, stall generator, constraints and all three placement
options. The worst option-0 path now lies inside the unchanged divider
remainder recurrence, rather than the register-file/operand-select cone.
At unchanged 4,194,434 CoreMark cycles, 59.313 MHz predicts
about 141.41 iterations/second, 15.45 percent above 122.48. Acceptance
requires fitness strictly above 128.11408, approximately 53.737 MHz.
Forecast 15 percent with medium confidence; mapping sensitivity and
incorrect prospective-producer qualification remain the main risks.

The combined prototype passed all seven existing unit-test runners and
five-program architectural/CRC cosimulation. Canonical stalled CoreMark
retained exactly 4,194,434 bracketed cycles, no OOB, all five canonical
CRCs and the required validation text. The early-selection RTL passed
all 53 standard ALTOPS formal checks; the combined variant differs only
by the register-file synthesis attribute, which changes no RTL semantics.
Re-run the unchanged correctness gates and vendor timing after final
implementation; these preliminary measurements are not an accepted eval.
Preserve nret=1, exact core IO, strict RVFI ordering, all trap checks,
bounded progress, nine-cycle division occupancy and every eval contract.

title: Pipeline high-half multiplication while forwarding the low product from EX
motivation:
The champion scores 122.48 at 51.374 MHz and 4,194,434 bracketed CoreMark
cycles. Its reported worst path runs from the register file through ID,
EX and u_alu to data memory (24.951 ns, 13 cells). A fresh unmodified
placement-option-0 timing run reproduced 50.874 MHz and confirmed that
this path traverses u_alu/mul_uu_63_s0/B[12] to DOUT[41], a multiplier
DSP arc with 3.780 ns cell delay. Full high-half multiplication and its
result selection therefore sit on an observed critical path.
Earlier structural changes successfully isolated division and registered
its magnitude before sign correction; the most recent attempt to register
raw divider operands instead created a slow preparation stage and regressed
to 44.144 MHz. Shift the structural focus to the still unregistered multiply
network. A reference trace has 93,960 multiplies inside the timing markers,
all low-half MUL, and 35,640 following instructions with matching raw
source indices. Deferring every multiply result would impose avoidable
bubbles on this workload. Preserve early low-half availability while
moving the more expensive high-half reconstruction across EX/MEM.
