raw divider operands instead created a slow preparation stage and regressed
to 44.144 MHz. Shift the structural focus to the still unregistered multiply
network. A reference trace has 93,960 multiplies inside the timing markers,
all low-half MUL, and 35,640 following instructions with matching raw
source indices. Deferring every multiply result would impose avoidable
bubbles on this workload. Preserve early low-half availability while
moving the more expensive high-half reconstruction across EX/MEM.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one structural change: an asymmetric two-stage multiply datapath
with an early low-half output. EX computes four small partial products and
the low 32-bit result; EX/MEM registers the partial products; MEM reconstructs
high-half results for MULH/MULHSU/MULHU. MUL retains its existing EX/MEM
forwarding and zero added latency. Keep single-issue, in-order retirement,
the existing stage count, divider schedule and 64-entry agree predictor.
Independent instructions still flow each cycle. Only an immediate consumer
of a high-half multiply gets the same one-bubble interlock as a load consumer.

Use four explicit signed 17x17 products that fit Gowin's 18-bit DSP inputs.
For each operand, represent the low 16-bit limb as a nonnegative 17-bit
value. Its high limb is a sign-extended 16-bit value only when that operand
is signed for the selected operation; otherwise zero-extend it. MULH signs
both high limbs, MULHSU signs only A's high limb, and MULHU signs neither.
MUL may use unsigned limbs because its low result is sign-independent.
Form LL=AL*BL, LH=AL*BH, HL=AH*BL and HH=AH*BH as signed 34-bit values;
pack them as {LL,LH,HL,HH} in a 136-bit EX/MEM field. Preserve the fully forwarded
original operands separately for RVFI. Do not compute any full-width
product combinationally in the ordinary ALU path.

For the early MUL result in EX, its low 16 bits are LL[15:0]. Its upper
16 bits are (LL[31:16] + LH[15:0] + HL[15:0]) modulo 2^16. Compute the
three-input sum with a 16-bit carry-save compressor followed by one
16-bit addition: s=x^y^z, c=((x&y)|(x&z)|(y&z))<<1, upper=s+c, explicitly
truncating c and upper to 16 bits. Feed {upper,LL[15:0]} into the ordinary
EX/MEM alu_result field only for ALU_MUL. The cross-product low bits are
independent of sign extension; no carry from the bottom 16 bits is lost
because the cross terms begin at bit 16. This avoids full 64-bit addition
and high-result selection before the early MUL register boundary.

In MEM form the product modulo 2^64 from LL + (LH << 16) + (HL << 16)
+ (HH << 32), with correct sign extension before shifting. Compress the
four aligned rows with two carry-save levels and one final carry-propagate
addition, rather than a serial chain of wide additions. Use rows
{{30{LL[33]}},LL}, {{14{LH[33]}},LH,16'b0},
{{14{HL[33]}},HL,16'b0}, and {HH[31:0],32'b0}. Compress the first three,
then compress that sum/carry pair with the fourth, and add the final pair.
Select bits [63:32] only for MULH/MULHSU/MULHU; ordinary MUL uses its
existing registered alu_result. Capture the chosen result in
MEM/WB on the same edge as an ordinary instruction in that slot. Inspect
inferred DSP mapping and actual register boundaries: the intended timing
cut must separate DSP multiplication from full-product reconstruction.

Derive the late-result classification from the registered ctrl.alu_op:
ALU_MUL < op <= ALU_MULHSU identifies the three high-half operations.
Their EX/MEM alu_result is not yet forwardable. Extend the existing
load-use interlock to valid high-half multiplies with nonzero rd, and
exclude only these unavailable multiply results from EX/MEM forwarding.
Ordinary MUL remains eligible for immediate forwarding without a bubble.
Keep the conservative raw source-index comparisons and the current
redirect-independent payload hold/flush policy. Following the inserted
bubble, consumers obtain the assembled result from MEM/WB using the normal
bypass. Ensure WB selects that same value for the register file and RVFI.
Do not silently fall through to an older matching WB writer while a newer
high-half multiply destination is pending; the hazard protocol must prevent such
a consumer from advancing.

Hold all partial-product state with EX/MEM during actual data-memory
backpressure, and clear or invalidate it with exactly the same bubble,
divider-drain, flush and reset rules as its instruction. A multiply itself
issues no data-memory request and must not stall merely because dmemReady
is low. Preserve MEM/WB's retained forwarding payload when valid clears
under a data-memory hold. Back-to-back independent multiplies must flow
without a global busy state. Dependent multiplies use a bubble only when
the producer is a high-half multiply.
Preserve exact-once retirement and store acceptance, trap behavior, x0,
decoder default-illegal discipline and the unchanged nret=1 interface.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, preserve the existing four multiply formulas
and send their results through the same result-availability/interlock
schedule as real multiplication. The prototype keeps the ALTOPS formula
in alu_result through EX/MEM and MEM/WB, while withholding the high-half
EX bypass and inserting its bubble exactly as in hardware. Retain ALU
unit-test coverage by moving
the real multiply vectors intact to an appropriate registered datapath
test, with additional signed-high and cross-limb carry cases. Arithmetic
correctness needs real-operation tests because default formal uses ALTOPS.

Validate directed producer/multiply/consumer chains for ALU, branches,
JALR, load addresses and store data; same-rd overlapping writers; x0;
load-to-multiply and multiply-to-DIV dependencies; independent and dependent
consecutive multiplies; and both bus stalls. Check original RVFI operands,
result data, monotonic order, reset and squashed instructions. Run the
unchanged formal gates and stalled CoreMark cosim with canonical CRCs,
required UART validation text, bounds and timing markers.

An isolated RTL prototype of this exact asymmetric decomposition measured
4,194,434 marker-bracketed cycles and median Gowin Fmax 54.036 MHz across
options 0/1/2 (51.078, 54.036, 54.036 MHz). Preliminary fitness is 128.8279,
5.18 percent above 122.48. Option-0 area is 3,526 LUT4s and 867 registers,
with 8 LUT-RAMs, 6 BSRAMs and 2 DSPs. All canonical CoreMark CRCs, UART
validation text, markers and memory bounds passed. Selftest and three
random programs each passed full RVFI cosim both with and without bus
stalls (eight passes). An independent arithmetic model passed 100,484
signed/unsigned partial-product and carry-save comparisons. Formal gates
have not been run on this prototype; these remain required at implementation.

The all-multiplies-late alternative measured 53.906 MHz but 4,230,003
cycles, only 4.05 percent fitness improvement, below acceptance. The
early MUL path is essential to the proposed design. Forecast 5 percent
with medium confidence: the measured margin is small and implementation
must reproduce the register placement, signed widths and early result.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 128.11408, or about 53.737
MHz at the measured cycle count. Recheck actual cycles and median Fmax.
Principal risks are a different ALU operation actually limiting timing,
the unchanged divider becoming critical, synthesis moving the intended
registers, MEM reconstruction becoming critical, and dependency bubbles
outweighing the frequency gain. Evaluate median Gowin Fmax times measured
bracketed iterations/cycle, not path delay or Fmax alone.

title: Register bank-decoded training events for the 64-entry agree predictor
motivation:
The current 64-entry agree predictor already removes most recoverable
branch bubbles. Prior experiments established local saturating updates
and validity-only recovery as useful, while the most recent improvement
was dominated by Gowin Fmax rather than fewer direction misses. In this
session, the unchanged champion reproduced its 51.374 MHz median exactly.
Smaller tables, one-bit agreement, shared confidence and LUT RAM storage
all failed to beat its fitness. The strongest completed predictor
prototype instead retimed the training distribution into eight banks,
keeping all 64 independent two-bit counters and their direction lookup.
This is the single proposed angle: isolate late EX training feedback
from counter update decoding with a registered bank selection.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the existing 64-entry agree table indexed by PC[7:2], exact B/J
target prediction, weak-agreement reset state and locally saturating
counters. Add one stage only to predictor training, with eight registered
one-hot bank enables, a three-bit registered row index, and one registered
agreement bit. At every non-reset edge set bank_q to train_valid ?
(8'b1 << train_index[5:3]) : 8'b0. Capture row_q=train_index[2:0] and
agree_q=train_agree only when train_valid is asserted. On reset clear
all bank enables, row and agreement state, and reset every counter to
2'b10 as before.

Counter entry e consumes the PREVIOUS cycle's event when bank_q[e/8]
is set and row_q equals e%8. Increment its current local counter toward
3 for agree_q=1, decrement toward 0 otherwise. Preserve the original
binary saturating-counter implementation; no shared counter read mux,
state encoding change, capacity reduction or direction hash is proposed.
The new register boundary splits EX resolution and high-bank decoding
from the local row decode and saturating counter transition. It costs
12 additional state bits while reducing combinational control sharing
between the frontend table and late EX feedback.

The event register must accept one resolved branch every cycle and apply
one pending event every cycle, including consecutive aliases. Clear bank
validity on cycles without a new event; holding it would train repeatedly.
An already captured event applies despite current imem stalls, dmem stalls,
divider activity or a younger redirect. It represents an older branch
that already advanced. Reset cancels pending training with priority over
all table writes. Keep existing EX train_valid, train_index and train_agree
qualifications unchanged. Do not add training backpressure to the CPU.

Fetch reads the current pre-edge table state. Delaying training can change
nearby predictions, but the accepted instruction still carries its actual
predicted_taken bit, so existing EX mismatch recovery remains authoritative.
No bypass of a pending update, speculative history or rollback is needed.
Keep PC priorities, legal/aligned direct targets, unpredicted JALR,
validity-only squashes, raw decode inputs and all pipeline payload holds.
Do not modify arithmetic, ALTOPS scheduling, decoder defaults, trap behavior,
RVFI ordering, memory handshakes, nret=1 or any evaluation contract.

An isolated prototype of exactly this eight-bank implementation measured
50.713, 50.975 and 50.975 MHz across the three vendor placement options;
median Fmax was 50.975 MHz. Area was 3,197 LUT4s and 751 registers, versus
3,277 and 739 for the champion, with unchanged 8 LUT RAMs, 6 BSRAMs and
6 DSPs. Canonical stalled CoreMark retained exactly 4,194,434 bracketed
cycles, completed with both markers, no OOB, all five expected CRCs and
the required validation text. Calculated fitness was 121.5301 iter/sec,
0.78 percent BELOW 122.48. This prototype therefore does not establish
an improvement and does not clear the 128.11408 acceptance threshold.
The forecast is deliberately negative rather than claiming an unsupported
five-percent gain. This is the best completed predictor-only candidate
from the investigation, not a measured winning replacement.

After implementation, reproduce the median Gowin measurement and run the
unchanged formal and architectural cosim gates. The preparation experiment
was a timing/CoreMark prototype, not a completed formal qualification.
The main limitation is that the measured critical path still traverses
register-file/forwarding and execute arithmetic outside the predictor;
training retiming may not improve that limiting path sufficiently.

title: Two radix-4 divider digits with off-path divisor-multiple preparation
motivation:
The champion scores 140.57 at 58.960 MHz with 4,194,434 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path is now remainder_q to
remainder_q inside u_div: 22.507 ns arrival through 123 cells. The
four serial full-width restoring subtract/select steps are therefore
a directly observed timing target. Prior micro_opt hyp-20261001-001-r2s0
replaced four radix-2 steps with two radix-4 digits and gained 14.79%
on its older parent, but lost that round to completion retiming. The
current champion already incorporates completion retiming and shorter
operand selection, making the recurrence worth revisiting. The failed
raw-operand preparation experiment r4s1 cautions against moving more
serial arithmetic onto capture or a newly overloaded preparation cycle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one local arithmetic optimization in div_unit.sv: compute each
full-width four-bit iteration as two radix-4 digits with parallel trial
subtraction, and prepare the required 3D multiple outside that recurrence
and outside the operand-capture path. Keep the current first-nibble
capture, seven subsequent iteration edges, registered unsigned final
result, and sign/transfer cycle. All existing quotient and remainder
register values must remain bit-identical at every corresponding edge.

Preserve the existing launch calculation and divisor_q capture. At
iteration_q==0, only eight dividend bits will have been consumed after
this edge: the current remainder is at most 15. Perform four explicitly
narrow restoring steps using an 8-bit trial/remainder and a 9-bit
subtraction against divisor_q[7:0], consuming quotient_q[31:28].
If any divisor_q[31:8] bit is set, D>=256, so instead append quotient
nibble zero and set remainder to {remainder_q[3:0],quotient_q[31:28]}.
Otherwise append the narrow recurrence's four quotient bits and retain
its remainder. For D=0, the narrow recurrence produces quotient nibble
15 and retains the consumed dividend prefix, just as the existing logic.
On this same iteration-zero edge, independently register the exact
34-bit value three_d_q = {2'b0,divisor_q} + {1'b0,divisor_q,1'b0}.
The 3D adder starts from the registered divisor and does not feed the
narrow remainder calculation. It is not added after operand forwarding
and signed magnitude conversion on the launch path.

At iteration_q values 1 through 6, replace the four serial radix-2
steps with two radix-4 digits. For each digit form the unsigned 34-bit
trial T={R[31:0],Q[31:30]}. Form exact 34-bit D and 2D by wiring from
divisor_q and use registered three_d_q for 3D. Compute three 35-bit
unsigned differences {1'b0,T}-{1'b0,kD}, k=1,2,3, in parallel. Bit 34
is the underflow bit. Select the largest k without underflow, otherwise
k=0 and T. Derive mutually exclusive enables directly from the three
underflow bits b1,b2,b3: pick3=!b3, pick2=b3&&!b2,
pick1=b2&&!b1, pick0=b1. Use a masked-OR data selection rather than a
chain of priority data muxes or separate compare-then-subtract logic.
The two quotient bits are {pick2|pick3,pick1|pick3}; append these
to Q[29:0]. For D!=0 the selected remainder
is below D and fits 32 bits; preserve full trial and multiple widths
until selection. D=0 selects digit three and leaves the prefix intact.
Register the state after both digits on the same existing edge.

Do not change start/busy/done/accept, ignored starts while busy, reset
cancellation, blocked completion, EX occupancy, original RVFI operands,
sign flags or final correction. Preserve divide-by-zero quotient
0xffffffff and remainder equal to the dividend, signed truncation toward
zero, dividend-signed remainder and INT_MIN/-1. Preserve the ALTOPS
formulas and the identical nine-cycle schedule in real and ALTOPS
builds. Reset the new multiple register and use it only after its
iteration-zero capture. No pipeline, predictor, IO or nret change is
needed, and no additional division cycle or early-out is proposed.

An isolated RTL prototype implementing this exact decomposition passed
the existing divider suite in real and ALTOPS builds, including exact
nine-cycle scheduling, per-edge quotient/remainder checks, changed
inputs while busy, reset cancellation and held completion. An independent
fixed-width arithmetic model checked 210,840 intermediate states over
30,120 unsigned operand pairs, including the 255/256 boundary and all
four radix-4 digits. Full RVFI cosimulation passed selftest and three
random programs both with and without bus stalls, eight passes total.
These checks supplement, rather than replace, the required formal and
real-arithmetic correctness gates.

The prototype measured Gowin Fmax 63.770, 62.587 and 62.587 MHz across
placement options 0/1/2: median 62.587 MHz. Option-zero area is 3,763
LUT4s and 736 registers, with 40 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs.
CoreMark completed in the unchanged 4,194,434 marker-bracketed cycles
under both bus stalls; the evaluator's canonical CRC, UART validation,
memory-bounds and marker checks passed. Preliminary fitness is 149.2144,
6.15% above 140.57. Forecast 6% with medium confidence: the margin above
the 4.6% threshold is modest and implementation must reproduce the
measured circuit. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 147.03622,
approximately 61.6734 MHz at unchanged cycles.

Timing supports the intended mechanism: the reported recurrence path
is no longer worst. Option zero is limited by WB/EX/ALU to data memory,
and options one/two by operand selection into divider launch. Further
recurrence improvements may therefore be capped by those unchanged
cones. Other risks include six subtractors increasing routing/divisor
fanout and the phase-selection mux. The full formal suite was not run
during hypothesis preparation and remains required during implementation.
Preserve all gates and judge the final median vendor Fmax times measured
bracketed iterations/cycle, not just the local divider path.

title: Distribute division across registered phases with a two-bit launch
motivation:
The champion scores 140.57 at 58.960 MHz and 4,194,434 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path is internal to div_unit:
remainder_q to remainder_q, 22.507 ns and 123 cells. Four serial
full-width restoring steps share one feedback register boundary.
Earlier structural work successfully separated unsigned completion
from sign correction without adding cycles. Registering raw operands
and doing eight serial prefix steps in one preparation cycle instead
regressed to 44.144 MHz; high-half multiply pipelining also failed to
clear acceptance. The proposed structural change distributes divider
work and state across dedicated register boundaries, reducing both
launch work and full-width arithmetic depth at unchanged latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the shared quotient/remainder feedback datapath with eight
dedicated phase register banks inside the existing blocking divider.
Bank zero captures two quotient bits at launch. Seven subsequent
phases consume 6,4,4,4,4,4,4 bits, leaving cumulative consumed counts
2,8,12,16,20,24,28,32 in banks zero through seven. Each phase reads
only its predecessor bank and writes its own successor bank. There
is no phase-selected quotient/remainder feedback mux in the timed
arithmetic path. The final bank feeds the existing separate sign
correction and completion/acceptance logic. This is one structural
divider repartition, not a change to pipeline issue or retirement:
only one division is active and EX occupancy remains exactly nine
cycles including launch and transfer.

On start && !busy, capture the same forwarded operand magnitudes A
and D and sign/operation flags as today. Compute only the top two
dividend bits N=A[31:30]. If any D[31:2] bit is set, initialize q2=0
and r2=N. Otherwise use two explicitly two-bit restoring steps with
three-bit subtraction/borrow results on D[1:0]. D=0 naturally yields
q2=3 and r2=N. Set Q[0]={A[29:0],q2}, R[0]={30'b0,r2}, divisor_q=D,
and iteration_q=0. Do not put a full-width 3D adder on this launch
path. Reducing launch from four bits to two is essential: an earlier
prototype with a four-bit launch remained limited by operand routing
through launch arithmetic.

Implement the six-bit phase with three parallel-trial radix-4 digit
steps and each four-bit phase with two such steps. Parallel here
refers to simultaneous subtraction of D,2D,3D within one digit;
successive digits still depend on the selected previous remainder.
For phase p=0..6, let c=2 for p=0 and c=4+4*p otherwise. Its bit
count n is six for p=0 and four otherwise. Let P=c+n and W=P+2.
Thus phase arithmetic widths W are 10,14,18,22,26,30,34. Each bank
can be declared as 32-bit Q/R and synthesis can prune constant bits.

A consumed prefix bounds R below 2^c, including D=0. Zero-extend
R[p][c-1:0] to W bits and start the phase's quotient shifter at Q[p].
For P<32, detect large_D=OR(divisor_q[31:P]); when true, the whole
phase has quotient digits zero and its remainder is simply the
extended dividend prefix. For P=32, large_D is false. Build d1 by
zero-extending divisor_q[P-1:0] to W bits, and d2=d1<<1.
For phase zero only, compute the narrow W-bit d3=d1+d2 locally.
In parallel with phase zero, register the exact full 34-bit 3D as
{2'b0,divisor_q}+{1'b0,divisor_q,1'b0}. Subsequent phases use the
low W bits of this registered triple. The large_D bypass makes
truncation harmless when D exceeds that phase's prefix bound;
otherwise all three divisor multiples are represented exactly.
Never form full 3D repeatedly in the dependent digit recurrence.

At each radix-4 step form the W-bit trial
T={Rstep[W-3:0],Qstep[31:30]}. Compute W+1-bit unsigned differences
{1'b0,T}-{1'b0,d1}, -d2, and -d3 simultaneously. Select the largest
non-borrowing multiple, or zero if all three borrow. Use mutually
exclusive enables and a masked OR of the corresponding difference
or unmodified trial, not a serial priority mux over result data.
Append the selected two-bit digit to Qstep[29:0]. With D=0 select
digit three, leaving the dividend prefix in the remainder.
At the phase edge, if large_D is true, write Q[p]<<n and
(R[p]<<n)|(Q[p]>>(32-n)); otherwise write the last digit network's
Q and zero-extended or truncated-to-32-bit R. The selected remainder
fits 32 bits. Keep intermediate trials and multiples at their full
stated widths.

Give each successor bank its own resettable always_ff update,
enabled only by active_q && !complete_q && iteration_q==p.
Bank zero updates only at accepted launch; banks one through seven
hold until their corresponding phase executes. During phase zero,
capture triple_divisor_q with the same active phase qualification.
On seven recurrence edges iteration_q advances from zero to seven;
done then asserts and the existing next edge transfers the corrected
result. Final magnitude selection must read Q[7]/R[7] directly.
An indexed current-bank view may be exposed for test observation,
but must not feed execution or final result selection. Retain
result_q/complete_q when accept is low and cancel every phase on
reset. Do not resample forwarded operands while busy.

Preserve signed truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainder,
INT_MIN/-1 results, all-ones quotient and original dividend remainder
for divisor zero. Preserve existing ALTOPS formulas and exactly the
same real/ALTOPS schedule. Keep EX metadata capture, forwarding,
older-stage draining, bus stalls and exact-once retirement intact.
Keep nret=1, top-level ports, decoder legality, predictor, multiplier,
ordinary ALU and every evaluation invariant unchanged.

A temporary RTL prototype of this precise banked 2+6+4+4+4+4+4+4
schedule measured median Gowin Fmax 62.001 MHz across placement
options 0/1/2: 60.632,62.001,62.001 MHz. Option-zero resources were
5,176 LUT4s, 1,070 registers, 40 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs.
Its worst reported option-zero path moved out of the divider to
MEM/WB through forwarding and the ALU to data memory. Stalled
CoreMark completed in exactly 4,194,434 bracketed cycles, passing
all canonical CRCs, validation text, memory bounds and timing
markers. The resulting preliminary fitness is 147.81732, a 5.16
percent gain over 140.57. Real and ALTOPS divider suites and the
existing pipeline suite passed. Selftest and three random programs
each passed full RVFI cosimulation both with and without bus stalls,
for eight passing cosim cases. Formal gates were not run on this
prototype and remain required during implementation.

Preserve all existing exact arithmetic and handshake coverage.
Update internal prefix-state expectations to 2,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,
comparing the active phase's state to independent integer division
of the consumed prefix. Add divisors immediately around the prefix
bounds 2^2,2^8,2^12,2^16,2^20,2^24,2^28, large-divisor bypass cases,
three-times-divisor overflow-width cases, and digit-boundary borrows.
Retain signed extremes, zero divisors, random full-width vectors,
changing request inputs while busy, reset in every phase, completion
backpressure and exact nine-cycle completion. Run unchanged formal
and pipeline gates, including ready-bus retirement progress.

Forecast five percent with medium confidence. Acceptance requires
fitness strictly above 147.03622, corresponding to 61.67338 MHz if
cycles remain unchanged; the measured margin is narrow. Reproduce
the stated register boundaries and arithmetic widths and remeasure
actual median Fmax times bracketed iterations/cycle. Main risks are
extra bank/divisor routing, synthesis reintroducing shared next-state
selection, a launch or multiplier path limiting frequency, and
implementation differences consuming the approximately half-percent
margin over the acceptance threshold. Do not claim a robust gain
from option-zero timing or divider arithmetic depth alone.

title: Eight-entry folded-PC agree predictor with local saturating updates
motivation:
The current predictor contains 64 locally updated two-bit agreement
counters indexed by PC[7:2]. Prior training retiming left CoreMark cycles
unchanged and regressed timing. Smaller direct-index tables were also
unsuccessful on the previous champion. This proposal instead combines a
much smaller table with ordinary XOR-folded address indexing, evaluated
on the current champion with its retimed operand selection and distributed
register file. It targets predictor circuit size while limiting systematic
low-address aliasing, without touching the arithmetic bottleneck.

An independent interpreter profile found 529,588 conditional branches and
only 13,735 JALR returns among 2,922,016 instructions in the canonical timed
region. Therefore a return stack alone has too little cycle headroom.
The proposed compact agree predictor was the best measured predictor-only
prototype in this investigation, although its gain is below acceptance.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 64x2 agree table with exactly eight independent two-bit
saturating counters indexed by fetch_index = pc[4:2] XOR pc[7:5]. Compute
train_index using the resolving branch's own in.pc[4:2] XOR in.pc[7:5].
This is one compact predictor architecture: fold adjacent word-address
fields to avoid making every branch separated by 32 bytes share an entry,
while reducing counter state from 128 to 16 bits and the direction mux
from 64:1 to 8:1. Use this ordinary address function for every program;
no hard-coded branch PCs, program signatures, phase detection or workload
specific initial contents. Narrow the training index consistently to
three bits in IF, EX and core wiring.

Preserve binary counter encoding and reset every counter to 2'b10, weak
agreement with backward-taken/forward-not-taken bias. Increment locally
with saturation when branch_taken equals the B-immediate sign, decrement
otherwise. Fetch reads only the selected MSB. For a legal conditional
branch with an aligned exact target, predicted_taken remains counter[1]
== imem_data[31]. Retain the existing legal-branch predecode, unconditional
aligned JAL prediction, unpredicted JALR and exact B/J target adder. Do not
add history, tags, a target table, a return stack, delayed training, new
pipeline stages, or a shared indexed training read/modify/write datapath.

Train exactly once per valid legal non-faulting conditional branch
advancing out of EX under the unchanged !reset, !stall and !execute_busy
conditions. Use that branch's folded PC and the current local counter;
never use the fetch PC or a saved counter snapshot. A simultaneous lookup
and update uses the pre-edge prediction and ordinary nonblocking update
semantics. Bubbles, held instructions, jumps, traps and squashed fetches
cannot train. Keep train_agree and train_valid logic unchanged.

Carry the same actual predicted_taken bit through the existing pipeline.
Exact direct targets still permit the existing one-bit mismatch recovery.
Preserve reset/redirect/accept/hold PC priority, validity-only squashes,
raw instruction and source-index paths, ID/EX metadata holds, load-use
interlocks, divider scheduling, memory backpressure and retained forwarding
operands. Leave all arithmetic, ALTOPS behavior, decoder legality, nret=1,
top-level IO, architectural RVFI fields/order and evaluation contracts
unchanged. No core_pkg or additional hazard logic changes are required.

The isolated prototype completed canonical CoreMark with both bus stalls
in 4,221,451 marker-bracketed cycles, versus 4,194,434 for the champion:
27,017 additional cycles, or approximately 0.64 percent. Both markers,
all five expected CRCs, required UART validation text and no out-of-bounds
accesses were observed. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 59.219,
59.924 and 59.924 MHz; median Fmax is 59.924 MHz versus 58.96 MHz. Option-0
area was 3,212 LUT4s and 590 registers versus 3,501 and 702, with 40 LUT
RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs. Its worst reported path runs from retained
MEM/WB load data through forwarding into divider launch; the arithmetic
paths remain the limiting concern.

Calculated prototype fitness is 141.95119 iter/sec, approximately 0.983
percent above 140.57. This DOES NOT clear the required 147.03622 iter/sec
acceptance threshold. At the measured cycle count, acceptance would require
median Fmax above 62.07062 MHz. Forecast one percent with low confidence,
not an unsupported five percent gain. These are preliminary timing and
CoreMark results, not completed formal qualification or an accepted
replacement. The prototype changes a real predictor circuit; nevertheless,
its timing gain is too small to distinguish confidently from placement
sensitivity under the tournament's acceptance rule.

After implementation, reproduce actual bracketed cycles and median Gowin
Fmax, run unchanged formal and architectural cosim gates, and retain all
canonical CRC, UART, bounds, liveness and RVFI checks. Update the independent
prediction oracle to eight counters and the three-bit fold. Add directed
low-index conflicts that separate after folding, deliberate folded
collisions, every index, opposite-bias aliases, saturation, same-index
concurrent lookup/update, reset and held/squashed branch cases. Retain all
existing architectural assertions and imem/dmem/divider stall coverage.
Principal risks are increased interference in the very small table,
workload sensitivity and an unchanged divider-limited Fmax ceiling.

implementation_notes:
# Eight-entry folded-PC agree predictor

Implemented the proposed predictor in `cores/bench/rtl/if_stage.sv`,
`ex_stage.sv`, and `core.sv`. The bank contains exactly eight independent
binary two-bit counters, reset to `2'b10`, with local saturating updates.
Fetch selects only the counter MSB using `pc[4:2] ^ pc[7:5]`; EX trains using
the resolving instruction's `in.pc[4:2] ^ in.pc[7:5]`. Both interfaces and
the core training wire are three bits. `train_valid` and `train_agree` are
unchanged. No architectural deviations from the proposed RTL change.

Updated the independent cycle-level predictor oracle in
`cores/bench/test/test_pipeline.py` to eight counters and folded indices.
Added directed tests for eight PCs spaced 32 bytes apart that separate after
folding, and all 64 combinations of the two three-bit address fields.
Adapted deliberate collision chains to PCs 16/52/88 and destructive
opposite-bias aliases to PCs 16/52. Retained the 256-byte alias test.
Checks cover both saturation limits, concurrent lookup/update with pre-edge
prediction, all counter contents on every edge, reset, held/squashed
instructions, exact-once training/retirement, legality/alignment, metadata
holds, memory backpressure, and divider behavior. Existing architectural,
operand, and cycle-stamped regression assertions remain enabled.

## Local validation

- Required Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings or errors.
- `pytest -q cores/bench/test`: PASS, seven runners, 101 cocotb cases,
  including 34 pipeline cases and real/ALTOPS divider coverage.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh`:
  PASS on the first attempt, 53 checks passed, zero failures. The script
  automatically selected the unchanged single-retirement wrapper/config.
  No counterexample and no RTL fix attempts were needed. This is the
  standard ALTOPS formal gate; formal-deep was not run.
- `make cosim TARGET=bench NRET=1`: PASS for both ELFs. Selftest RVFI was
  compared with the unchanged ISS both with and without bus stalls;
  canonical CoreMark passed with both bus stalls. The initial bare
  `make cosim TARGET=bench` failed at C++ compilation because build.sh
  defaults to NRET=2. Supplying the existing NRET=1 setting fixed invocation
  without editing any contract file or changing the core's ports.
- The unchanged `tools.eval.fpga.run_coremark_ipc` helper reports completed
  execution, 10 iterations, 4,221,451 marker-bracketed cycles, and
  2.3688537424691178e-6 iterations/cycle. Both markers, completion, bounds,
  canonical UART validation and all five CRCs passed: seedcrc=e9f5,
  crclist=e714, crcmatrix=1fd7, crcstate=8e3a, crcfinal=fcaf.
- `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`: all three vendor
  synthesis/place/route runs passed, using the unchanged timed wrapper and
  stall generator. This runs the timing command's flow with every placement
  option so the scored median can be reported.

| Gowin placement option | Fmax (MHz) |
| --- | ---: |
| 0 | 58.558 |
| 1 | 59.867 |
| 2 | 59.867 |
| Median | 59.867 |

Option-0 area: 3,262 LUT4 logic cells, 590 registers, 40 LUT RAMs,
four BSRAMs, six DSPs; 26 reported logic levels. Its worst reported setup
path is within the divider, from `quotient_q_31_s1` to `remainder_q_0_s1`
(22.371 ns reported arrival time). Reports are generated under
`cores/bench/generated/timing/gowin_p{0,1,2}/impl/pnr/`.

## Result and concerns

The bracketed cycle count matches the hypothesis's prototype exactly:
27,017 cycles (about 0.64%) more than the champion's 4,194,434. Local timing
and LUT area differ from the preliminary prototype, so the measured values
above supersede its 59.924 MHz and 3,212 LUT figures for this implementation.

Calculated fitness is 141.81617 iterations/sec, approximately 0.887% above
the stated 140.57 champion. This does not meet the required 147.03622
iterations/sec acceptance threshold. At this cycle count, that threshold
requires more than 62.07062 MHz median Fmax. The compact table increases
aliasing, behavior remains workload-sensitive, and divider arithmetic still
limits timing. The observed sub-one-percent gain does not establish an
accepted replacement or a robust five-percent improvement.

Only the three predictor RTL files, the pipeline test file, and this
requested implementation note were edited. Decoder, arithmetic, hazards,
pipeline metadata, RVFI ports/order, nret=1, and evaluation contracts were
preserved.
lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-003-r6s2 (regression, +0.89%): Shrinking the agree predictor from 64 to eight locally updated counters indexed by pc[4:2] ^ pc[7:5] saved 239 LUT4s and 112 registers but increased CoreMark cycles by 0.64% through aliasing, while the unchanged divider critical path limited the fitness gain to less than 1%.

title: Separate the registered load/store address from the general ALU result
motivation:
The champion scores 153.96 at median Gowin Fmax 64.576 MHz and
4,194,434 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path runs
from MEM/WB through forwarding and u_alu into data memory. Prior
micro_opt work successfully shortened operand selection, and the
latest divider improvement shifted the bottleneck out of division.
Detailed vendor timing of a local result-mux prototype identifies
the multiplier DSP in this path. mem_stage drives dmem_addr directly
from the general EX/MEM alu_result, so every ALU operation feeds
the memory address cone even though loads and stores need only ADD.
A dedicated registered effective address should remove the multiply
result selection from that cone without changing execution timing.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split only the load/store address value from the general ALU-result
bus at the existing EX/MEM register boundary. Add a 32-bit
effective_addr field to ex_mem_t immediately after alu_result and
before write_data. On each normal valid EX advance,
set reg_q.effective_addr <= rs1 + in.imm, where rs1 is the existing
fully forwarded raw source and imm is the saved decoded immediate.
This is a local datapath and mux-fanout optimization. It adds no
stage, memory request, execution cycle, or instruction interlock.

The dedicated address adder must take those operands directly,
independent of ctrl.alu_op, the multiplier, divider result and
general ALU output selection. Do not derive the address from
alu_result and do not add an ALU/address selection mux after the
address register. Sharing identical addition logic is acceptable
only if the final memory address remains independent of operation
result selection. Use 32-bit modular addition, preserving all high
address bits and the two low byte-offset bits.

In mem_stage use in.effective_addr consistently for dmem_addr,
byte-lane masks, word/halfword alignment checks, load extraction
shift and aligned RVFI memory address. Keep reg_q.alu_result <=
in.alu_result for the ordinary nonload WB and forwarding path.
Keep original store data, load extension, mask qualification,
trap-suppressed writes, memory request enables and MEM/WB retention.
For every valid load/store, the new address equals the existing
ALU_ADD result exactly. Nonmemory instructions issue no memory
request; their otherwise unused address bus value may change.
Preserve full address width; never exploit benchmark address
limits to truncate or alias accesses.

effective_addr belongs to the complete EX/MEM payload. Hold it
with the memory operation during dmem backpressure, reset it with
the bundle and clear it when EX/MEM becomes a bubble. The division
metadata bundle is already cleared at launch, so division transfer
produces zero in this unused field and never issues a memory
operation. Preserve exact-once acceptance and retirement, load-use
and prospective forwarding rules, branch recovery, x0 behavior,
default-illegal decoding, nret=1 and top-level IO. Leave the general
ALU, M-extension arithmetic, ALTOPS formulas, nine-cycle divider
scheduling, predictor and register file unchanged.

CoreMark should retain 4,194,434 marker-bracketed cycles for the
same bus-stall sequence, so the gain must come from measured median
vendor Fmax. Forecast seven percent with medium confidence.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 161.04216,
approximately 67.55 MHz at unchanged cycles. Main risks are extra
adder/register routing, synthesis merging the cones again, or
divider and general ALU feedback timing limiting the new clock.
Judge the unchanged three-option Gowin median times measured
iterations/cycle, not the disappearance of a single critical path.

An isolated RTL prototype of exactly this three-file change measured
Gowin Fmax 64.613, 69.104 and 69.104 MHz for placement options 0/1/2,
median 69.104 MHz. Option-zero resources were 5,099 LUT4s, 1,102
registers, 40 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs, compared with
5,180 LUT4s and 1,070 registers for the champion. The worst path
moved from the multiplier-to-memory cone to WB/EX branch recovery
for option zero and to a general ALU-result register for options
one and two. Memory addressing remains fully functional and timed.

All 53 standard single-channel ALTOPS formal checks passed, including
legality, uniqueness, liveness and register consistency. The unchanged
pipeline suite passed. Selftest and three random
programs each passed full RVFI cosimulation with and without both
bus stalls, for eight passing trace cases. Stalled CoreMark passed
canonical CRCs, UART validation text, bounds and timing-marker
checks in exactly 4,194,434 bracketed cycles. Preliminary fitness
is 164.75167, 7.01 percent above 153.96 and above the 4.6 percent
threshold. These are hypothesis-preparation measurements; the
implementation must reproduce the circuit and rerun all gates.

title: Pipeline every multiply across EX and MEM with registered partial products
motivation:
The champion scores 153.96 at 64.576 MHz and 4,194,434 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path now starts at MEM/WB load data,
passes through WB, EX forwarding and multiplier DSPs, and ends at data
memory. A fresh option-zero Gowin report reproduced 58.685 MHz and
explicitly identified mul_ss, mul_uu and signed/unsigned DSP products
on the worst paths; multiplication is therefore a measured bottleneck.
The latest divider repartition removed the previous dominant bottleneck.
The ALU still computes full combinational products for every multiply.
The r5s1 structural attempt pipelined only high-half reconstruction and

path using the existing EX/MEM boundary: EX produces small DSP-sized
partial products, and MEM reconstructs the selected 32-bit result.
MUL, MULH, MULHU and MULHSU all become available at MEM/WB, like a load.
Independent instructions still issue each cycle; an immediately dependent
consumer receives the existing one-bubble load-use style interlock.
This is one structural repartition of multiplication. Preserve the
divider, predictor, issue width, retirement boundary and ordinary ALU.

Form four signed 17x17 products from 16-bit limbs. Low limbs are
zero-extended to 17 bits. Sign-extend A's high limb for MULH/MULHSU

Register the four signed 34-bit values LL, LH, HL and HH in EX/MEM

should remain before that register boundary. Preserve the fully
forwarded original operands separately for RVFI.

Pack the 136-bit EX/MEM field as {LL,LH,HL,HH}. In MEM reconstruct

C=((X&Y)|(X&Z)|(Y&Z))<<1, then compress S,C and the fourth row

Select bits 31:0 for MUL or 63:32 for the high operations

The low half must also use this registered-partial-product path.
Remove real combinational multiplication from the fast ALU instance.

younger-producer forwarding input. The hazard prevents capture of a

Do not add a combinational MEM-to-EX reconstruction bypass.

title: Single-bit agree prediction in native distributed RAM
motivation:
The current predictor uses 64 locally updated two-bit counters. Prior
training retiming and table downsizing did not overcome the arithmetic timing
limit. Canonical CoreMark has only about 46,342 conditional direction misses
in an independent sequential trace, so a larger history predictor offers
little cycle headroom. A one-bit last-agreement table eliminates the indexed
training read and saturating-counter logic, allowing the entire predictor
state to map to four native LUT-RAM primitives. This is a predictor storage
and update architecture change, with an explicit prediction-accuracy cost.

hypothesis.motivation:
The current predictor uses 64 locally updated two-bit counters. Prior
training retiming and table downsizing did not overcome the arithmetic timing
limit. Canonical CoreMark has only about 46,342 conditional direction misses
in an independent sequential trace, so a larger history predictor offers
little cycle headroom. A one-bit last-agreement table eliminates the indexed

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 64 two-bit agreement counters with one 64x1 distributed-RAM
last-agreement table. Keep fetch_index = pc[7:2] and train_index = in.pc[7:2].
Every qualified EX branch event writes train_agree directly into that entry;
there is no training read, hysteresis, counter arithmetic, history register,
new pipeline stage or prediction-metadata expansion. A branch predicts taken
when the selected agreement bit equals the B-immediate sign, still qualified
by legal branch encoding and exact target alignment. Preserve aligned JAL
prediction and unpredicted JALR.

Use synthesizable inferred distributed RAM with one asynchronous indexed
fetch read and one synchronous write port. Form one write address, one write
data and one write enable outside the memory process, then write only through
that port. Do not reset the array in a loop, which prevents RAM inference.
Reset a six-bit initialization index and an init_done flag. On each of the
next 64 non-reset edges write agreement=1 to the indexed row, setting done
on the edge that initializes row 63. Suppress training writes during scrub;
use static backward-taken/forward-not-taken predictions until done. Fetch,
JAL prediction, EX recovery and architectural retirement continue normally;
initialization must not stall the CPU. Reset disables the write port on its
edge and restarts the complete scrub even when asserted during initialization
or a simultaneous training event. Uninitialized table contents cannot affect
prediction before init_done. Initialize every entry identically for every
program, without program-specific addresses or signatures.

After scrub, write_index=train_index, write_data=train_agree and
write_enable=!reset && train_valid. Before completion use init_index,
constant one and !reset instead. Fetch reads the pre-edge bit, including on
a same-index update. Use the unchanged qualified training event, so invalid,
illegal, faulting, held and squashed instructions cannot update. Repeated
same-index events each apply once and naturally leave the last agreement.

Preserve exact immediate targets, actual predicted_taken metadata, existing
one-bit direction mismatch recovery, reset/redirect/accept/hold PC priority,
validity-only squashes, raw instruction/source-index paths, ID/EX holds,
load-use interlocks, divider scheduling, forwarding, memory handshakes,
arithmetic and ALTOPS behavior. Keep nret=1, all external ports, decoder
legality, RVFI fields/order and every evaluation contract unchanged.

An isolated prototype completed the canonical ten-iteration CoreMark run
with both bus stalls in 4,223,556 marker-bracketed cycles, versus 4,194,434:
a 0.694 percent cycle increase. The unchanged evaluation helper accepted all
five CRCs, required UART validation text, bounds, completion and both markers.
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 61.254, 63.306 and 63.306 MHz, versus
the champion's 64.576 MHz median. Option-zero resources were 4,904 LUT4s,
949 registers and 44 LUT RAMs, compared with 5,180, 1,070 and 40. Four BSRAMs
and six DSPs remained. The critical path still traversed retained load data
selection, EX forwarding and the ALU into the data-memory interface.

Calculated prototype fitness is 149.88791 iter/sec, 2.645 percent BELOW the
153.96 champion. This does not clear the 161.04216 acceptance threshold.
Forecast minus three percent with low confidence rather than claim a measured
winning improvement. The smaller predictor circuit is real, but the current
arithmetic-limited design does not turn that reduction into sufficient Fmax.
These are preliminary timing and CoreMark results, not a completed formal
qualification or an accepted replacement.

After implementation reproduce median Gowin Fmax and bracketed cycles and
run the unchanged formal and architectural cosim gates. Update the independent
predictor oracle for last-agreement semantics, all 64 initialization writes,
pre-edge lookup/update and exact-once training. Exercise reset during every
scrub phase, the transition to dynamic mode, repeated aliases, opposite-bias
branches, loop exits/re-entry and arbitrary imem/dmem/divider holds. Execute
well beyond 64 cycles so initialized dynamic prediction is covered even
though the standard short formal window remains in static fallback. Preserve
all architectural assertions; representation-specific tests must check the
new policy without discarding legality, alignment, ordering or stall coverage.
Principal risks are the extra loop-exit misses, destructive aliases, reset
scrub behavior and an unchanged arithmetic timing bottleneck.

title: Compare branch source candidates before forwarding selection
motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. A fresh Gowin option-zero run reproduces 71.996 MHz
and the worst path from ID/EX raw_rs1_mask[2] through EX to fetch PC.
The detailed path traverses the forwarded operand mux, a full-width
comparison carry chain and redirect control. Earlier r5s0 work moved
forwarding decisions into ID/EX, but a late high-fanout source-enable
still precedes branch comparison. Recent divider and multiply work has
exposed this branch path. Local shifter, writeback and address prototypes
did not clear the acceptance margin, so focus on removing the source
selection delay from the measured branch-comparison chain itself.

hypothesis.motivation:

CoreMark cycles. A fresh Gowin option-zero run reproduces 71.996 MHz
and the worst path from ID/EX raw_rs1_mask[2] through EX to fetch PC.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move conditional-branch source selection after comparison. Compute
one-bit branch predicates for each pair of existing forwarding source
candidates in parallel, and select the predicate using the two saved
one-hot source masks. This is one combinational EX datapath optimization;
keep pipeline boundaries, instruction latency and branch recovery timing.

Define A[0]=in.rs1_val, A[1]=fwd_ex_mem, A[2]=fwd_mem_wb, and similarly
B[0]=in.rs2_val, B[1]=fwd_ex_mem, B[2]=fwd_mem_wb. For each i,j in 0..2,
compute P[i,j] from the unchanged branch_op: equality for BEQ, inequality
for BNE, signed less-than/greater-or-equal for BLT/BGE, and unsigned
less-than/greater-or-equal for BLTU/BGEU. Reserved branch_op values must
retain a false predicate. Form branch_cond as a balanced reduction OR
of P[i,j] & in.raw_rs1_mask[i] & in.raw_rs2_mask[j]. Avoid a priority mux,
a forwarding mux before these comparators, or fresh EX tag comparisons.
A portable combinational function with the original six branch cases
and generated source-pair instances is a concrete implementation.

When both sources select the same shared forwarded bus, their operands
are identical: pairs (1,1) and (2,2) can constant-fold to true for BEQ,
BGE and BGEU and false for BNE, BLT and BLTU. Preserve these identities
and allow ordinary synthesis sharing of opposite comparisons. Do not
replicate whole ALUs or target adders. Retain the existing raw rs1/rs2
muxes for RVFI operand capture, JALR targets, division and store data.
The comparator matrix must read original candidate buses directly.

Use the new branch_cond in the existing branch_taken expression and
leave branch/jump targets, actual_taken, misalignment detection,
redirect qualification, prediction recovery and predictor training
unchanged. All valid executing branches already have exactly one source
selected in each registered mask; preserve that invariant, x0 and the
younger-producer priority. Do not qualify a candidate bus with current
WB valid or write enable: retained invalid MEM/WB data is a required
forwarding source during memory stalls. Invalid instruction payloads
remain unable to redirect, train or retire. Keep the unchanged nret=1
IO, decoder legality, load/multiply interlocks, divider schedule,
ALTOPS formulas, bus handshakes and exact retirement accounting.

This changes the late-mask path from operand mux then full comparison
to selection of already-computed one-bit predicates. Operand data can
begin comparison before source selection settles. The tradeoff is more
comparators, candidate-bus fanout and routing; WB data arrival, unchanged
redirect control, divider recurrence or memory arithmetic may instead
limit Fmax. The eight percent forecast is speculative, not a measured
gain. The proposal adds no cycles: expect 4,230,003 bracketed CoreMark
cycles with the same stall sequence. Acceptance requires fitness above
182.46424, approximately 77.185 MHz at that cycle count. Evaluate with
all three Gowin placement options and retain only a gain above 4.6 percent.

Retain existing tests and exercise all nine source-pair selections for
all six branches. Include equality, signed extrema, opposite signs,
unsigned high bits and low-bit differences that propagate across a
comparison carry chain. Check both operands forwarded from the same
producer, same-rd older/younger priority, x0, load/multiply-use bubbles,
completed division, and held WB data during prolonged dmem stalls.
Check actual next PC, original RVFI operands, predictor recovery and
training behavior, and exact-once ordered retirement. Exercise taken
misaligned targets and untaken branches with misaligned immediates.
Run unchanged standard formal and RVFI cosimulation gates and stalled
CoreMark CRC, UART, bounds and marker checks. Do not weaken any checks.

title: Rebalance divider launch and first recurrence to three plus five bits
motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Prior structural improvements removed shared divider
feedback and pipelined multiplication. The current divider consumes
two bits during launch, then six in its first registered recurrence;
that first recurrence cascades three radix-4 digits plus local 3D
preparation. Fresh vendor experiments repeatedly expose divisor_q to
remainder_bank[1] among the limiting paths after other cones improve.
Rebalance work across that existing register boundary without adding
execution cycles or disturbing the successful dedicated phase banks.

hypothesis.motivation:

CoreMark cycles. Prior structural improvements removed shared divider
feedback and pipelined multiplication. The current divider consumes

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change only the divider's internal bit partition from
2+6+4+4+4+4+4+4 to 3+5+4+4+4+4+4+4. Preserve all eight quotient/remainder
banks, seven recurrence edges, the final sign/transfer phase and exact
nine-cycle EX occupancy. This is a structural repartition of launch
versus first-phase arithmetic; leave the other pipeline stages,
branch predictor, multiplier, forwarding and memory system unchanged.

On accepted launch normalize operands exactly as today. Let A and D
be the unsigned magnitudes and N=A[31:29]. If any D[31:3] bit is set,
initialize q3=0 and r3=N. Otherwise compute three explicitly three-bit
restoring steps using D[2:0], a four-bit subtract/borrow result and an
initially zero remainder. Consume A[31], A[30], A[29] in order, append
each non-borrow decision and select the trial or difference. D=0 must
naturally produce q3=7 and r3=N. Capture Q[0]={A[28:0],q3} and
R[0]={29'b0,r3}, together with existing divisor, sign and operation
flags. Do not move full-width 3D preparation onto the launch path.

For phase zero set C=3, N=5, P=8 and W=10. Begin with one binary
restoring step, followed by the existing two parallel-trial radix-4
digits. Form the W-bit first trial by zero-extending
{R[0][2:0],Q[0][31]}, subtract zero-extended d1 using W+1 bits, select
by borrow, and shift the quotient by one. Feed this intermediate
quotient/remainder into two ordinary D/2D/3D radix-4 steps. Preserve
the existing 10-bit local d3 and the phase-wide D>=256 bypass; the
bypass shifts Q[0] by five and appends its five high bits to R[0].
Later phases retain their existing C,N,P,W values and recurrence.
The consumed-prefix sequence becomes 3,8,12,16,20,24,28,32.

Keep full 34-bit triple_divisor_q preparation parallel with phase
zero, so phases one through six still use registered exact 3D. Keep
the final registered unsigned magnitude, sign correction, divisor-zero
quotient override, INT_MIN/-1 behavior and completion retention.
Neither operand forwarding changes while busy nor completion stalls
may alter the captured request. Reset cancels every active operation.
Preserve original RVFI operands and the unmodified real/ALTOPS start,
busy, done and accept schedule; ALTOPS formulas remain unchanged.
Preserve nret=1, legality checks, memory handshakes, exact-once
retirement and the frozen formal retirement-progress bound.

The intended tradeoff moves one small restoring bit to launch and
replaces a radix-4 digit in the longest first recurrence with one
binary step. A temporary RTL prototype measured Gowin placement
options 0/1/2 at 68.454,74.223,74.223 MHz: median 74.223 MHz.
Stalled CoreMark retained exactly 4,230,003 bracketed cycles with
canonical CRCs, validation text and no out-of-bounds accesses.

This does not clear the required 182.46424 acceptance threshold;
the one-percent forecast is deliberately modest and is not a claim
of a qualifying replacement. Reproduce the implementation and vendor
measurement before drawing conclusions from this small difference.

independent checks at every registered prefix with the new launch
coverage, and the existing real/ALTOPS pipeline suites. Selftest and

without both bus stalls, for eight passing trace cases. Full formal
qualification remains required during implementation; results from

real-arithmetic divider tests, pipeline/cosim gates and canonical
stalled CoreMark. The principal risks are added launch delay and
ordinary ALU or branch recovery limiting Fmax after the first divider

title: Separate predicted and recovery PC registers without adding a miss cycle
motivation:
The champion's reported worst path starts at ID/EX raw_rs1_mask and ends
at the fetch PC, through EX and IF, after multiplier pipelining raised
median Fmax to 73.790 MHz. Prior table shrinking, training retiming and
one-bit RAM storage did not produce an accepted improvement. Keep the
successful 64-entry, two-bit agree predictor and improve its recovery
integration: the current PC register merges forwarded EX correction data,
normal predicted next-PC data and hold feedback at its input. Separate
storage for prediction and correction can remove this shared input mux
from the late EX target path without paying another misprediction cycle.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's reported worst path starts at ID/EX raw_rs1_mask and ends
at the fetch PC, through EX and IF, after multiplier pipelining raised
median Fmax to 73.790 MHz. Prior table shrinking, training retiming and
one-bit RAM storage did not produce an accepted improvement. Keep the
successful 64-entry, two-bit agree predictor and improve its recovery
integration: the current PC register merges forwarded EX correction data,
normal predicted next-PC data and hold feedback at its input. Separate
storage for prediction and correction can remove this shared input mux
from the late EX target path without paying another misprediction cycle.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the single fetch-PC storage register with two 32-bit registers,
predicted_pc_q and recovery_pc_q, plus one recovery_active_q bit. The
architectural fetch PC is a combinational selection between these registers:
pc = recovery_active_q ? recovery_pc_q : predicted_pc_q. Use this selected
PC consistently for imem_addr, out.pc, PC-relative prediction arithmetic
and the unchanged agree-table index. Keep IF/ID combinational, ID/EX and
EX resolution unchanged, and preserve the actual accepted predicted_taken
bit. This is one predictor-recovery storage architecture change.

On reset set both PC banks to RESET_PC and recovery_active_q to zero.
Otherwise, when !stall, capture the existing next_pc in predicted_pc_q.
Capture redirect_target in recovery_pc_q whenever !recovery_active_q OR
redirect. Thus the inactive correction bank can sample EX without a late
redirect-dependent enable, while an active correction bank holds its PC
through arbitrary instruction or pipeline stalls. A new redirect always
permits capture, even when the correction bank is already active.
Set recovery_active_q to one when redirect is asserted; otherwise clear
it on !stall and retain it on a stall. Reset has highest priority and
redirect has priority over stall for the bank selector and correction
capture. These are separate clocked assignments, not a reconstruction
of the original three-way next-PC mux ahead of either bank.

A resolving miss captures its target and selects the correction bank on
the SAME edge that currently updates the single PC register. The target
is therefore visible during the same next cycle, with no new miss bubble,
pending execution operation or delayed branch retirement. If the target
fetch stalls, keep the correction bank selected and stable. Once that
fetch is accepted, capture its predicted successor in predicted_pc_q and
select that bank on the same edge. A predicted-bank write during a redirect
is harmless because the correction bank becomes selected. Inactive-bank
sampling must never change the selected PC or create an instruction
acceptance, predictor training event or architectural side effect.

Preserve the existing PC next-state recurrence exactly: reset selects the
reset vector; a redirect selects redirect_target regardless of imem stall;
otherwise an accepted fetch selects its predicted next PC; otherwise the
selected PC holds. Do not rely on redirect and recovery_active_q being
mutually exclusive. Retain the explicit redirect capture case so even this
combination is correct. Leave raw imem data and source-index paths,
validity-only flushes, downstream stall qualification and recovery priority
unchanged. All counter lookup/update ordering, legal B/J predecode,
alignment suppression, JAL prediction and unpredicted JALR remain identical.
No target comparison, BTB, return stack, history table or pipeline register
stage is added. Keep nret=1, all IO, RVFI, decoder, memory, arithmetic and
ALTOPS contracts unchanged.

The intended timing split is EX target arithmetic into the dedicated
correction register, then a small registered-selector mux at fetch address.
Normal prediction arithmetic feeds its own register without the late EX
correction data input. The bank selector is only one bit. Expect roughly
33 additional storage bits before synthesis, rather than a second complete
instruction packet. The important risk is that moving a mux after the PC
register adds delay to PC-to-imem/decode and PC-relative prediction paths,
or an unchanged divider/ALU path becomes the frequency limit. Measure
Gowin timing; RTL mux counting alone cannot establish an improvement.

Use the existing independent predictor/operand oracle and retain all exact
cycle checks: ready-bus miss latency, prediction hit throughput, division
schedule and retirement gaps must remain unchanged. Add directed bank
transition checks for reset, redirect coincident with imem-not-ready,
several stalled cycles while a correction PC is active, release into both
sequential and predicted-taken successors, consecutive control transfers,
forwarded JALR targets, opposite-direction misses and training/read aliases.
Check selected-PC hold on data stalls and divider holds, exact-once
retirement and memory effects, illegal/misaligned transfers and arbitrary
inactive-bank values. Run unchanged formal, full RVFI cosim and canonical
CoreMark validation with both bus stalls and marker-bracketed cycles.

Acceptance requires fitness above 182.46424 iter/sec. If the champion's
4,230,003 CoreMark cycles are preserved, median Fmax must exceed
77.182428 MHz. An isolated prototype of this exact split-PC design measured Gowin Fmax
of 67.836, 70.355 and 70.355 MHz across placement options 0/1/2: median
70.355 MHz. CoreMark took exactly 4,230,003 marker-bracketed cycles with
both bus stalls, matching the champion, and passed canonical CRC, UART,
bounds and marker validation. Calculated fitness is 166.32376 iter/sec,
4.65274 percent below 174.44, so this prototype DOES NOT meet acceptance.
The negative-five-percent forecast reflects this measured regression;
do not present the original timing rationale as an observed speedup.

The prototype passed all 53 unchanged nret=1 ALTOPS formal checks,
including liveness, register consistency, PC continuity, legality and
unique retirement, using isolated staging of the original wrapper and
check properties/depths. All 38 existing pipeline tests passed unchanged,
including exact-cycle checks and the independent predictor/operand oracle.
Selftest and three random programs passed full RVFI cosimulation both
with and without bus stalls, eight passing cases. Real-arithmetic
formal-deep was not run; no arithmetic logic changes in this proposal.

Placement option zero used 5,431 LUT4s and 1,247 registers versus 5,422 and
1,214 for the champion, with 40 LUT RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs unchanged.
Its reported worst path now ends at an agree counter, not a PC register;
options one and two likewise end in counter training. The PC-bank change
therefore moves the reported limiting path, but the remaining feedback and
arithmetic timing does not yield a net frequency improvement. Submit this
one bounded predictor-recovery hypothesis with that limitation explicit.
Reproduce the implementation and its full metric before any acceptance;
retain the champion unless the unchanged threshold is actually exceeded.

title: Balanced LUT comparison tree for conditional branch resolution
motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 CoreMark iterations/second at median Gowin
Fmax 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003 bracketed cycles. Its reported worst path
starts at ID/EX raw_rs1_mask[2] and ends at the fetch PC through EX:
19.184 ns arrival and 38 cells. The r8s0 hypothesis describes a forwarded
operand comparison carry chain on this path, but its speculative
source-pair comparator matrix produced no measured improvement. The
r8s2 split-PC experiment regressed. Instead, shorten the ordering
comparator itself without moving source selection or pipeline boundaries.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 CoreMark iterations/second at median Gowin
Fmax 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003 bracketed cycles. Its reported worst path
starts at ID/EX raw_rs1_mask[2] and ends at the fetch PC through EX:
19.184 ns arrival and 38 cells. The r8s0 hypothesis describes a forwarded
operand comparison carry chain on this path, but its speculative
source-pair comparator matrix produced no measured improvement. The
r8s2 split-PC experiment regressed. Instead, shorten the ordering
comparator itself without moving source selection or pipeline boundaries.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the conditional-branch comparison network in ex_stage.sv
with an explicit balanced lexicographic tree of two-bit comparisons.
Continue to compare the existing fully forwarded rs1 and rs2 buses.
This is one combinational micro-optimization: no prediction changes,
source-pair speculation, extra stage, instruction latency or miss cycle.

Partition each 32-bit operand into sixteen two-bit groups, numbered
from least significant to most significant. For each group compute
equality E and unsigned less-than L directly from its four input bits.
For group bits a1,a0 and b1,b0, use
E = ~(a1 ^ b1) & ~(a0 ^ b0), and
L = (~a1 & b1) | (~(a1 ^ b1) & ~a0 & b0).
Each leaf predicate fits a LUT4. Combine adjacent low/high groups with
E_parent = E_high & E_low and
L_parent = L_high | (E_high & L_low).
Use four explicit balanced reduction levels, 16->8->4->2->1, rather
than a serial fold or a full-width relational/subtraction expression.
The root yields equality and unsigned less-than. Signed less-than is
(rs1[31] ^ rs2[31]) ? rs1[31] : unsigned_less_than.

Map BEQ/BNE to equality/inverted equality, BLT/BGE to signed less-than
and its inverse, and BLTU/BGEU to unsigned less-than and its inverse.
Keep reserved branch_op values false. Express the tree as local wires
and constant generate loops in ex_stage.sv so no source-list or module
interface changes are required. Preserve the existing raw operand
muxes and their saved one-hot controls, x0 behavior, younger-writer
priority and retained MEM/WB data forwarding during stalls. Do not gate
these forwarded buses with current WB validity or write enable.

Leave branch_taken, target adders, misalignment handling, actual_taken,
advancing, redirect and predictor training equations unchanged. Keep
ALU SLT/SLTU and all multiply/divide datapaths unchanged; this proposal
specifically attacks the branch comparator on the measured EX-to-PC
path. Preserve all decoder legality rules, nret=1 IO and RVFI accounting,
bus handshakes, load/multiply interlocks and divider/ALTOPS schedules.

The expected timing benefit is replacing a full-width ordering carry
dependency with one leaf LUT plus four small combination levels before
branch selection. The two-bit leaf equations make the intended LUT4
implementation explicit. Inspect the vendor mapped path to confirm
synthesis retained the balanced structure. Routing, operand fanout or
another arithmetic path may erase the benefit.

An isolated prototype measured 70.126, 70.568 and 70.568 MHz across
Gowin placement options 0/1/2, with median 70.568 MHz. This is below
the champion, not a demonstrated improvement. At unchanged CoreMark
cycles the projected fitness is 166.8273, a 4.364-percent regression.
Option zero used 5,338 LUT4s and 1,214 registers and moved the worst
path to the first divider recurrence. All 38 existing pipeline tests
passed unchanged. A combinational SAT proof established exact predicate
equivalence for every operand pair and branch function. Full formal
and CoreMark validation remain required during implementation.

CoreMark should retain 4,230,003 marker-bracketed cycles with the same
stall sequence. Measure all three Gowin placement options and the full
canonical CoreMark validation. Acceptance requires fitness strictly
above 182.46424, corresponding to about 77.183 MHz at this cycle count.
Retain the champion if the measured gain does not exceed 4.6 percent.

Preserve existing tests and add directed checks for every branch funct3
using equal operands and first differing bits at every bit position,
including each two-bit group boundary. Exercise equal high prefixes
with conflicting lower groups, opposite signs, signed extrema and
unsigned high-bit values. Cover all existing forwarding source pairs,
same-producer operands, same-rd older/younger priority, x0, load/multiply
dependencies, completed division and prolonged simultaneous bus stalls.
Check original RVFI operands, taken/untaken next PCs, misaligned taken

title: Register the first divider phase's narrow 3D multiple at launch
motivation:
The champion reaches 174.44 iter/sec at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior structural work distributed the
divider's quotient/remainder banks and moved full-width 3D preparation
alongside the first recurrence. However, phase zero still computes
its own narrow 3D before three serial radix-4 digits. Recent vendor
experiments repeatedly expose divisor_q to remainder_bank[1] as a
limiting path. The r8s1 three-plus-five bit repartition gained only
0.59 percent. Retiming the narrow multiple itself across the launch
boundary is a distinct way to remove work from that first recurrence.

hypothesis.motivation:

bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior structural work distributed the
divider's quotient/remainder banks and moved full-width 3D preparation

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 10-bit prefix_triple_q register to the real divider datapath.
On start && !busy, capture exactly
  {2'b0, divisor_magnitude[7:0]}
  + {1'b0, divisor_magnitude[7:0], 1'b0}.
Reset this register to zero and otherwise retain it until another
accepted launch. In phase p=0, drive the existing W=10 d3 wire directly
from prefix_triple_q, replacing its combinational d1+d2 expression.
This is one structural retiming of narrow multiple preparation across
the existing operand-capture boundary. Do not change quotient-bit
allocation, radix, arithmetic phase banks or execution latency.

The width is deliberate: phase zero produces an eight-bit consumed
prefix. For D<256, 3D<=765 fits exactly in ten bits, so the saved value
is the exact multiple needed by all three first-phase radix-4 digits.
For D>=256, retain the existing |divisor_q[31:8] large-divisor bypass
of the entire recurrence. In that case its truncated multiple must
never select the architectural next quotient or remainder. Do not
replace the full divisor with its low byte or change the bypass test.

Keep the existing full 34-bit triple_divisor_q generation during
iteration zero, parallel with the first recurrence. Phases one through
six continue to use this registered full-width multiple exactly as
before. Full-width 3D must not move into operand capture; only the
ten-bit first-phase value moves. Use explicitly narrow zero-extended
operands for the new addition, avoiding a 32/34-bit multiply or adder
followed by truncation. Use the existing signed/unsigned magnitude
result so negative signed divisors, including INT_MIN, remain correct.

Preserve the original 2+6+4+4+4+4+4+4 consumed-bit partition, nine-cycle
EX occupancy, sign/exception handling, completion retention and
start/busy/done/accept protocol. Launch captures the fully forwarded
request exactly once; changing source operands during execution must
not alter prefix_triple_q. Reset cancels execution and clears its new
state. Keep all real and ALTOPS formulas and scheduling identical to
the champion. No changes to forwarding, ordinary ALU, multiplication,
predictor, memory buses, decoder legality, RVFI, nret=1 or formal
properties/depths are part of this hypothesis.

The intended timing trade is a short extra launch-side adder in
exchange for removing local multiple generation from the first
three-digit recurrence. The launch-side sum only consumes the low
eight magnitude bits and does not depend on upper-bit carry output.
An unchanged forwarding/ALU/address path can become the new limit;
removing one divider adder does not guarantee a qualifying gain.

A prototype of exactly this retiming measured Gowin placement options
0/1/2 at 71.606, 74.330 and 74.330 MHz, giving median 74.330 MHz.
Option zero used 5,422 LUT4s and 1,223 registers, versus 5,422 and
1,214 for the champion; LUT RAM, BSRAM and DSP counts were unchanged.

marker-bracketed cycles, with all CRCs, validation text and bounds
checks passing. Calculated fitness is 175.72092 iter/sec, only
0.7343 percent above 174.44. This measured candidate DOES NOT exceed
the required 182.46424 acceptance threshold. The one-percent forecast
below reflects this small measured gain, not a claim of replacement.
Worst reported paths moved into existing forwarded ALU/address logic.

existing real/ALTOPS pipeline suites, including independent prefix
arithmetic, captured operands, predictor behavior, exact-cycle checks,
reset, completion backpressure and the ten-cycle ready-bus retirement
bound. Selftest and three random programs passed full RVFI cosimulation
both with and without stalls, eight passing trace cases. All 53
unchanged nret=1 ALTOPS formal checks also passed, using isolated
staging with the original wrapper, properties and depths. Real-M
formal-deep was not run; the real divider suite checks the changed
arithmetic. Repeat the required qualification gates on implementation.

Preserve all existing tests. Add directed first-phase cases around
D=0,1,2,3,255,256,257 and signed equivalents, every two-bit launch
prefix, radix-4 decision boundaries, maximum first-byte prefixes and
large divisors whose low byte aliases a small divisor. Independently
check saved narrow 3D and the first successor Q/R state against the
captured magnitude and integer division. Cover request mutation,
reset and consecutive differing divisors. Reproduce the full vendor
median and validated CoreMark metric during implementation; retain
the champion unless the unchanged 4.6-percent threshold is exceeded.

title: Compact 32-entry Gray-encoded agree predictor
motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 iter/sec at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior eight-entry prediction increased
aliasing, while one-bit RAM lost useful hysteresis. Use a middle-sized
32-entry agree predictor with full two-bit hysteresis and a Gray state
encoding that simplifies its late training feedback. This bounded predictor
replacement targets lookup fan-in, training fanout and local update logic
together while preserving the existing pipeline and recovery architecture.

hypothesis.motivation:

marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior eight-entry prediction increased
aliasing, while one-bit RAM lost useful hysteresis. Use a middle-sized
32-entry agree predictor with full two-bit hysteresis and a Gray state

replacement targets lookup fan-in, training fanout and local update logic
