hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 64 binary agree counters with 32 locally updated two-bit
Gray-encoded agree entries. This is one compact predictor design, with no
BTB, return stack, history predictor, additional pipeline stage or change
to recovery timing. Use fetch_index = pc[6:2] ^ {4'b0,pc[7]}.
Keep the existing six-bit EX train_index = in.pc[7:2] and all core ports;
inside if_stage fold it identically as train_index[4:0] ^
{4'b0,train_index[5]}. Use the five-bit folded index in each of the 32
local write-enable comparisons and the 32-to-1 prediction lookup.

Store prediction_q, the predicted agreement with backward-taken/forward-
not-taken, and weak_q, whether that prediction has weak confidence. Map
ordinary saturating states 00,01,10,11 to (prediction_q,weak_q)
00,01,11,10 respectively. Reset both bits to one, reproducing the existing
weak-agreement initial state 2'b10. On a qualified local training event,
set weak_q <= train_agree ^ prediction_q. Update prediction_q <= train_agree
only when the OLD weak_q is one; otherwise retain prediction_q. Both use
pre-edge state. Unselected entries retain both bits, and reset wins over
training. Use legal identifiers such as weak_q, since weak is reserved.
Drive agreements[entry] directly from prediction_q.

All eight local state/outcome transitions are exactly equivalent to the
original two-bit saturating counter. Confidence remains weak when a weak
prediction changes direction; an outcome matching the old prediction makes
it strong. This retains hysteresis while replacing increment/decrement and
terminal-state decoding with one confidence-qualified direction update and
one XOR. There are 64 state bits, half the current table's storage, and a
32-way lookup. Keep storage and update logic local to each entry; do not
introduce RAM, a shared indexed training read or delayed training events.

Retain the existing branch bias, legal B/J predecode, alignment checks,
immediate target calculation, predicted_taken capture, direct JAL prediction
and unpredicted JALR. Leave the single PC register, EX actual resolution,
validity-only recovery, raw instruction/source paths, load/multiply hazards,
DIV/REM schedule and memory handshake behavior unchanged. Keep nret=1,
all RVFI fields, exact-once retirement and every hard invariant. New aliases
may change predictions and cycle counts, but may never change architectural
results, accepted-training discipline or redirect priority over fetch stalls.

Keep the independent binary-counter test oracle. Adjust only its table
size, reset length, folded index and observed-state decoding: reconstruct
binary state as {prediction_q,prediction_q XOR weak_q}. Its saturating
transition algorithm, architectural checks, exact-cycle requirements for
unchanged datapaths and stall/flush assertions stay intact. Test all eight
transitions and both saturated endpoints, both PC[7] fold values,
destructive aliases, simultaneous lookup/update, reset/update priority,
held branches, wrong-path instructions and data/instruction stalls.

below 174.44. This is not a qualifying improvement; the forecast records

title: Remove branch-direction feedback from prospective write qualification
motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003 CoreMark
cycles. Recent micro_opt branch-comparison rewrites failed to clear the
acceptance margin. Detailed Gowin reports from isolated local trials
expose a WB-to-EX-to-forwarding-to-ID path as well as EX-to-PC paths.
In ex_stage, misalign_fault includes the full forwarded branch predicate
and suppresses ctrl_with_trap.reg_write. That flag also drives
next_reg_write and prospective source-mask generation in decode.
Conditional branches already have reg_write=0 from validated decode,
so their direction and target alignment unnecessarily enter this
register-write qualification cone. Use that exact instruction-class
invariant to remove the false control dependency.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003 CoreMark
cycles. Recent micro_opt branch-comparison rewrites failed to clear the
acceptance margin. Detailed Gowin reports from isolated local trials
expose a WB-to-EX-to-forwarding-to-ID path as well as EX-to-PC paths.
In ex_stage, misalign_fault includes the full forwarded branch predicate
and suppresses ctrl_with_trap.reg_write. That flag also drives
next_reg_write and prospective source-mask generation in decode.
Conditional branches already have reg_write=0 from validated decode,
so their direction and target alignment unnecessarily enter this
register-write qualification cone. Use that exact instruction-class
invariant to remove the false control dependency.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Separate EX trap reporting from destination-write suppression by
instruction class. Keep misalign_branch, misalign_jump and misalign_fault
exactly unchanged, including their full branch/jump predicates and target
alignment checks. Initialize ctrl_with_trap from in.ctrl as today, set
ctrl_with_trap.is_illegal when misalign_fault is true, but clear
ctrl_with_trap.reg_write only when misalign_jump is true. In concrete
terms, move the reg_write=0 assignment out of the if(misalign_fault)
block and place it under a separate if(misalign_jump). Keep
next_reg_write = in.valid && ctrl_with_trap.reg_write unchanged.

This relies on a property of the existing decoder, not a new assumption:
every reachable ctrl with is_branch=1 has reg_write=0. Both legal
conditional branches and reserved branch encodings cannot write an rd;
reserved encodings retain the default illegal controls. Therefore
in.ctrl.reg_write && !misalign_fault is architecturally identical to
in.ctrl.reg_write && !misalign_jump for every reachable instruction.
A taken misaligned branch still reports a trap and has no destination
write, since the decoded write flag was already zero. A misaligned JAL
or JALR still loses its link-register write. Aligned jumps, ordinary ALU
operations and all M-extension operations keep their original write flags.
Keep every illegal-decoder default and validated opcode/funct arm intact.

The timing opportunity is specific: remove the 32-bit forwarded branch
comparison, branch-taken logic and branch-target qualification from the
write-enable signal used by prospective forwarding. The shorter signal
continues through the existing younger/older tag matches and registered
source masks. This reduces a late EX-to-ID feedback path and the fanout
of the branch predicate without changing comparator arithmetic, source
priority, prediction, stages, instruction latency or recovery timing.
No additional registers or timing constraints are needed.

Leave actual_taken, redirect, redirect_target, predictor training,
pc_next, branch metadata and all fault reporting unchanged. Do not
suppress branch misalignment traps or redirect a faulting branch. Keep
memory misalignment handling in MEM, x0 exclusion, trap-qualified jump
forwarding, load/multiply bubbles, division capture/completion, retained
WB forwarding during dmem stalls, all ready/hold priorities, nret=1 IO
and exact retirement ordering. Leave real multiply/divide and ALTOPS
formulas and scheduling unchanged. Do not apply the simplification to
arbitrary unconstrained control-bit combinations: prove it through the
unchanged instruction decoder and full-core formal model.

Forecast an unmeasured six percent fitness gain with low confidence.
Other EX-to-PC, general-ALU/address and divider paths may limit the gain;
this is a targeted control-cone hypothesis rather than a demonstrated
fitness improvement. At unchanged 4,230,003 CoreMark cycles, acceptance
requires fitness above 182.46424, about 77.183 MHz median Gowin Fmax.
Measure all three placement options and retain the unchanged canonical
CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks. Run standard formal and RVFI
cosimulation; verify the branch comparison no longer feeds prospective
register-write qualification in the vendor netlist.

Keep all existing tests and add a decoder property that every legal
conditional branch has is_branch=1 and reg_write=0, while reserved branch
funct3 values stay illegal and side-effect-free. Test taken and untaken
misaligned branches of all six conditions with both forwarding operands,
and branch instruction bits[11:7] deliberately matching the following
instruction's source so a spurious prospective writer is detected.
Check aligned/misaligned JAL and JALR link writes, including a younger
consumer of the suppressed rd, older/younger same-rd priority and held
MEM/WB data under simultaneous bus stalls. Check identical RVFI traps,
source operands, destination writes, next PCs and ordered retirements.
Preserve every existing assertion and exact-cycle/progress check.

An isolated prototype of this exact EX control change passed the
existing decoder unit-test runner, real-arithmetic pipeline runner
and ALTOPS multiply pipeline runner without changing their assertions.
These checks include the existing trap, forwarding, stall and exact
retirement-cycle coverage. Full standard formal, canonical CoreMark
validation and final vendor timing remain implementation gates.

title: Decouple instruction fetch with a one-entry fall-through buffer
motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Recent structural divider retimings improved
fitness by less than one percent as other timing paths became
limiting. The current frontend freezes the request PC on every
backend hold, discarding opportunities to accept a ready instruction
during load/multiply interlocks, data-bus stalls and division.
A small elastic boundary between fetch and decode can use those
idle slots to hide later instruction-bus stalls without adding a
compulsory pipeline stage or changing the predictor algorithm.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Recent structural divider retimings improved
fitness by less than one percent as other timing paths became
limiting. The current frontend freezes the request PC on every
backend hold, discarding opportunities to accept a ready instruction
during load/multiply interlocks, data-bus stalls and division.
A small elastic boundary between fetch and decode can use those
idle slots to hide later instruction-bus stalls without adding a
compulsory pipeline stage or changing the predictor algorithm.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one fall-through instruction buffer in if_stage. Keep the PC
register as the next instruction-bus request address; buffer a
separate decode-head PC, instruction and predicted_taken snapshot.
When empty, decode sees the live bus response combinationally,
preserving current zero-wait latency. When occupied, decode sees
the buffered tuple and can advance even if io_imemReady is low.
This is one structural frontend-decoupling change. Keep the
champion's backend, arithmetic, predictor table and training rules.

Export fetch_available = buffer_valid || io_imemReady. Pass this
availability to the hazard unit in place of physical imem ready
for decode starvation; backend hold, late-use and redirect behavior
otherwise retain their current priorities. Hazard comparisons and
prospective forwarding tags MUST use the selected decode-head
instruction, not raw io_imemData, because the bus can now address
the following instruction. Select head payload using only buffer
occupancy, independently of redirect, flush and decode validity.
Use separate continuous assignments for
payload and validity so no artificial packed-bundle combinational
dependency feeds flush back into the source-index comparisons.

Let stall be the existing frontend stall output after the above
availability change. Outside reset/recovery, fetch_accept is
io_imemReady && (!buffer_valid || !stall). Advance the request PC
only on fetch_accept, using the existing prediction computed from
that request PC and its actual bus instruction. If fetch_accept
and (buffer_valid || stall), capture the bus tuple into the buffer
and set buffer_valid. This covers an empty buffer accepting during
a backend hold and simultaneous consume/refill of an occupied
buffer. Otherwise, if !stall, clear buffer_valid: a buffered head
has drained without refill or an empty-buffer response bypassed
straight into decode. Otherwise retain the buffer. Never overwrite
a full buffer while its head is held. The buffer must support one
instruction per cycle under continuous ready buses.

Recovery has final priority: install redirect_target as the request
PC, invalidate the buffer and squash the younger ID/EX validity.
Discard any same-edge speculative response logically, by clearing
buffer_valid. Crucially, redirect must NOT gate the 65-bit buffer
payload capture enable: capture PC/instruction/prediction with its
ordinary fetch_accept && (buffer_valid || stall) enable, and reset
it deterministically. A wrong-path tuple may be written on recovery
but remains invalid. Implement validity reset/redirect priority in
a separate assignment. This avoids placing late EX recovery on
every payload clock-enable pin. Reset returns the request PC to
zero and empties the buffer. An instruction-bus stall alone
must not discard a valid buffered head. A backend hold may capture
at most the available buffer capacity; it must not launch, retire
or train a buffered instruction early. Save predicted_taken when
the response is fetched, including simultaneous predictor training,
and use that saved bit when the head reaches EX. Recomputing its
prediction on dequeue would associate it with a different table
state and break direction recovery. Keep direct-target alignment
checks, JALR recovery and one training event per advancing branch.

Preserve exactly one ordered RVFI retirement, original instruction
PCs and raw operands, x0, illegal/misalignment traps, stable blocked
data-memory requests and exact-once stores. Preserve all multiply
and divider arithmetic, ALTOPS formulas, nine-cycle DIV occupancy,
load/multiply dependency interlocks and the frozen ready-bus
retirement-progress bound. Keep nret=1 and every external port.

A temporary one-entry prototype reduced canonical stalled CoreMark
from 4,230,003 to 4,022,833 marker-bracketed cycles, a 5.15-percent
improvement in iterations/cycle, with canonical CRCs, validation
text and no out-of-bounds accesses. Selftest and three random
programs each passed full RVFI cosimulation with and without both
bus stalls. With validity-only recovery and the payload enable
specified above, placement options 0/1/2 measured 73.803, 71.956
and 71.956 MHz: median 71.956 MHz. This gives 178.86897 iter/sec,
about 2.54 percent above the champion, below the required 4.6-percent
threshold. These preliminary measurements do not establish an
acceptable champion replacement. The extra head mux and control
fanout still consume part of the cycle savings.

The initial buffer protocol passed all 53 unchanged nret=1 ALTOPS
formal checks. The validity-only refinement changes only invalid
payload capture; rerun all checks on the final implementation.
An adapted independent queue/operand model passed the real pipeline
tests apart from two deliberately unrun champion-specific timing
snapshot cases; those snapshots still require architectural updates.
The existing multiply-filtered ALTOPS pipeline tests also passed.
Do not treat partial test-model adaptation as completed qualification.

Update frontend test reference models to track the independent
request PC and queued decode head, accepted responses, saved
predictions, simultaneous dequeue/refill, and recovery cancellation.
Existing cycle snapshots assume fetch PC equals decode PC and that
imemReady alone determines decode validity; replace those obsolete
scheduling expectations with an independent elastic-frontend model,
retaining full RVFI, operand, memory, arithmetic, predictor-training,
reset and progress assertions. Do not drop correctness coverage to
accommodate changed instruction-fetch timing. Test buffer empty/full,
downstream stalls, imem stalls during buffered issue, saved prediction
changes, producer priority, reset while full, recovery while full
and wrong-path load/store/divide cancellation. Trigger directed
data-memory holds from the intended active bus request rather
than an assumed fetch-PC position, retaining the required coverage
of MEM/WB forwarding data surviving invalidation during a hold.

Run unchanged formal and architectural cosim gates and the adapted
pipeline tests. Reproduce canonical stalled CoreMark and vendor
timing. Acceptance still requires fitness strictly above 182.46424
iter/sec; at 4,022,833 cycles this needs about 73.40 MHz. The forecast
reflects the preliminary measured gain; it is not a claim that
this circuit already clears the acceptance threshold.

title: Parallel branch predicates for same-cycle predictor recovery
motivation:
The champion's reported worst path starts at a registered forwarding mask and
ends at the fetch PC through EX branch resolution. Prior counter-table
shrinking, Gray encoding and separate PC storage failed to clear the
threshold. The existing checker selects 32-bit forwarded operands before
comparing them, putting forwarding selection and comparison in series. Branch
prediction recovery can instead select between precomputed one-bit outcomes,
without extending recovery or changing the divider's already tight bounded
liveness schedule.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's reported worst path starts at a registered forwarding mask and
ends at the fetch PC through EX branch resolution. Prior counter-table
shrinking, Gray encoding and separate PC storage failed to clear the
threshold. The existing checker selects 32-bit forwarded operands before
comparing them, putting forwarding selection and comparison in series. Branch
prediction recovery can instead select between precomputed one-bit outcomes,
without extending recovery or changing the divider's already tight bounded

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the conditional-branch prediction checker in EX with parallel
prospective-source comparisons followed by a one-bit selection. This is one
predictor-recovery architecture change. Retain the existing 64-entry agree
predictor, direct B/J targets, saved predicted_taken bit, single PC register,
unpredicted JALR, and same-cycle EX recovery/training. No additional pipeline
stage, miss cycle, table change or arithmetic-unit optimization is proposed.

Define three rs1 candidates as in.rs1_val, fwd_ex_mem and fwd_mem_wb, and
three rs2 candidates as in.rs2_val, fwd_ex_mem and fwd_mem_wb. Evaluate the
decoded branch condition independently for every candidate pair before
forwarding selection. Pair (i,j) is selected by in.raw_rs1_mask[i] AND
in.raw_rs2_mask[j]. OR the nine pair outcomes masked by those enables to
produce branch_cond. The existing one-hot masks retain younger-producer
priority and choose exactly one pair for a valid instruction. Compare the
original sources directly; never feed the predicate units from already-muxed
rs1 or rs2 buses.

Each pair evaluates BEQ/BNE, BLT/BGE and BLTU/BGEU with the exact existing
signed and unsigned semantics; reserved branch_op values yield false. Express
equality once and unsigned less-than once per pair, derive signed less-than
from differing signs or unsigned less-than, and share complementary outcomes
within each pair. Keep independent unsigned less-than expressions for the
two reversed EX/MEM and MEM/WB pairs; explicit reciprocal sharing measured
worse timing in a separate prototype.
Keep the shallow selected-outcome OR explicit. Do not replace the source
masks, create an indexed operand mux ahead of a shared comparator, or impose a
new reset, valid or WB-write-enable gate on forwarded data.

Keep ordinary forwarded rs1/rs2 and independent ALU operand selection
unchanged for ALU, JALR, stores, multiply/divide, and RVFI. Use the selected
branch_cond in the existing branch_taken, actual_taken, redirect and
train_agree equations without changing any qualification or latency. Direct
target arithmetic and alignment checks remain unchanged. A correct prediction
still accepts its successor without a bubble; a direction miss still squashes
exactly the current fetched instruction on the same advancing EX cycle.
Preserve deferred resolution during older dmem stalls, divider holds, recovery
priority over imem stalls, valid-only flushing and MEM/WB data retention.

The intended benefit is moving the wide compare alongside forwarding
selection, shortening the path from saved forwarding controls into prediction
checking, PC recovery and predictor training. Multiple comparisons cost area
and increase source-data fanout; unchanged divider and ALU paths can limit the
clock. Preserve the original recovery latency: adding a recovery stage can
violate the unchanged bounded-liveness check on a redirect to DIV.

An isolated nine-pair prototype passed all 53 unchanged nret=1 ALTOPS formal
checks, the 38 existing pipeline tests plus their multiply ALTOPS runner, and
full-RVFI comparison of selftest and three random programs both with and
without bus stalls. A combinational SAT proof established exact branch
condition equivalence for every operand value, every branch_op, and every
legal pair of one-hot forwarding masks. Canonical stalled CoreMark retained
exactly 4,230,003 marker-bracketed cycles, all five CRCs, validation text,
completion and in-bounds operation.

That prototype measured 66.254, 71.444 and 71.444 MHz across Gowin placement
options 0/1/2, median 71.444 MHz. Option zero used 5,755 LUT4s and 1,214
registers with unchanged LUT RAM, BSRAM and DSP counts. Calculated fitness is
168.89823 iterations/second, about 3.18 percent below the 174.44 champion. The
limiting paths include forwarded ALU/data-memory and fetch recovery. Thus this
tested implementation does NOT qualify; the forecast records its measured
limitation. The three-comparison variant using already-forwarded rs2 was worse
and is not proposed.

Retain the champion unless the final implementation's measured median Gowin
Fmax times canonical CoreMark iterations/cycle exceeds 182.46424
iterations/second. At unchanged 4,230,003 cycles, this requires Fmax above
77.18243 MHz. Do not change arithmetic units, the table, verification gates or
benchmark to compensate for this predictor experiment's timing limitations.

Preserve nret=1, all top-level ports and RVFI fields, decoder legality,
misalignment traps, exact-once retirement, memory handshakes, real and ALTOPS
arithmetic, and every invariant. Prove combinational equivalence of selected
branch_cond to comparing the original forwarded operands for all operand
values, all branch_op values and all nine legal one-hot source combinations.
Run the existing pipeline predictor and operand monitors unchanged, the
unchanged formal suite and full-RVFI cosim, then canonical stalled CoreMark
validation and all three Gowin placement options.

title: Remove result-selection muxes from forwarded memory addressing
motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 iter/sec at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent critical paths start at retained
MEM/WB load data, pass through WB selection and forwarded EX arithmetic,
and terminate at data memory. The prior r7s0 dedicated-address experiment
gained 7.01 percent against the pre-multiplier-pipeline champion but was
outscored by the multiplier retiming. The current champion still routes
addresses through the general ALU result. Optimize this one forwarded
address cone at both existing register boundaries, removing result-type
selection before and after effective-address addition.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 iter/sec at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent critical paths start at retained
MEM/WB load data, pass through WB selection and forwarded EX arithmetic,
and terminate at data memory. The prior r7s0 dedicated-address experiment
gained 7.01 percent against the pre-multiplier-pipeline champion but was
outscored by the multiplier retiming. The current champion still routes
addresses through the general ALU result. Optimize this one forwarded
address cone at both existing register boundaries, removing result-type
selection before and after effective-address addition.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Preselect final writeback data at the existing MEM/WB input, and give
load/store effective addresses a dedicated EX/MEM register fed directly
by fully forwarded rs1 plus the decoded immediate. These are coordinated
mux-placement changes along the same WB-to-EX-to-memory address cone.
Add no stage, request buffer, execution cycle or new interlock.

Replace only mem_wb_t's separate alu_result and read_data payloads with
one 32-bit writeback_data field. In MEM, select extended load_data if
in.ctrl.mem_to_reg, otherwise multiply_result if is_multiply, otherwise
in.alu_result. Use three exclusive enables and a masked OR before the
register: load_sel=mem_to_reg, mul_sel=!load_sel&&is_multiply,
alu_sel=!load_sel&&!is_multiply. Capture the final value with the original
MEM/WB enable. wb_stage drives w_data directly from writeback_data,
without a validity, reg_write, rd or result-type mux. Keep architectural
w_en=ctrl.reg_write&&valid and w_addr=rd. Real/ALTOPS multiply selection,
raw RVFI memory data and all source/PC metadata remain unchanged.

Add a 32-bit effective_addr field to ex_mem_t. On each ordinary valid
EX advance, capture rs1+in.imm directly, using the existing fully
forwarded raw rs1 and 32-bit modular addition. Keep the general
alu_result, partial products and write_data unchanged. The address must
not depend on ALU opcode/result selection, jump-link selection or the
divider completion-result mux. In MEM use effective_addr for dmem_addr,
byte masks, alignment checks, load-extraction offsets and aligned RVFI
memory address. Preserve all 32 address bits, including both byte-offset
bits. For an active load/store, this value equals the old ALU_ADD result.
An inactive memory address bus may differ, without issuing a request.

Use the original reset, valid, stall and completion priorities for both
bundles. EX/MEM effective_addr holds through dmem backpressure and is
cleared with the existing whole-bundle bubbles and divider metadata.
MEM/WB hold_wb must clear only valid, retaining writeback_data and all
metadata even after the old instruction retires. Otherwise capture data
also for invalid slots, matching the previous WB mux's behavior. Never
gate forwarding data with current WB valid or architectural write enable.
The same wb_w_data bus continues to serve EX, register-file write-first
bypass and RVFI destination data. Preserve saved source-mask priority,
x0 semantics, prospective write qualification, load/multiply-use bubbles,
captured division operands, all trap suppression and exact RVFI ordering.

This targets one combinational path: registered final WB value through
existing one-hot rs1 forwarding and a dedicated address adder into the
address register. Moving load selection before MEM/WB removes its late
mux; bypassing general execution-result selection removes the mux after
address arithmetic. Consolidating two WB data registers offsets the new
32-bit address register. The costs are earlier selection on the MEM
load/multiply inputs and possible changes in adder sharing and routing.
The unchanged divider and branch-recovery paths may cap the gain.

An isolated prototype of exactly this combined cone change measured
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 at 70.677, 75.082 and 75.082 MHz: median
75.082 MHz. Option zero used 5,427 LUT4s and 1,213 registers, versus the
champion's 5,422 and 1,214; LUT RAM, BSRAM and DSP counts were unchanged.
The worst reported path moved to existing branch/predictor-training
logic. The individual writeback and dedicated-address variants reached
73.136 and 71.284 MHz median respectively, supporting evaluation of the
complete forwarded-address cone rather than either local mux alone.

At unchanged 4,230,003 CoreMark cycles, the combined result implies
177.4987 iter/sec, 1.75 percent above 174.44. This does NOT meet the
required 4.6-percent acceptance margin. Forecast two percent with medium
confidence, reflecting the measured candidate rather than an unsupported
eight-percent claim. Acceptance still requires fitness strictly above
182.46424 iter/sec, approximately 77.183 MHz at those cycles. Reproduce
all three placement options and canonical stalled CoreMark with exact
CRCs, UART validation, bounds and timing brackets. Retain the champion
unless the unchanged threshold is exceeded. Keep nret=1 IO, decoder
legality, progress and every correctness gate.

In isolated staging using the unchanged nret=1 wrapper, properties and
depths, 52 of 53 standard ALTOPS formal checks had passed when this
hypothesis was finalized. The register-consistency check was still
running, with no failure reported. Full formal completion remains an
implementation gate; this is not a claim that the complete suite passed.

The prototype passed the unchanged real-arithmetic pipeline runner and
ALTOPS multiply-pipeline runner. Full RVFI cosimulation passed selftest
and three random programs both with and without simultaneous bus stalls,
eight passing cases total. Canonical CoreMark retained exactly 4,230,003
marker-bracketed cycles, with all CRCs, required validation text and
bounds checks passing. Real-M formal-deep was not run; these results
must not be described as a formal proof of real multiply/divide math.

Retain existing tests and cover forwarded load/store base addresses,
positive/negative offsets, wraparound arithmetic without issuing OOB
requests, byte lanes, half/word alignment traps, both operand sources,
same-rd priority and x0. Exercise ordinary ALU, load, jump-link, all four
multiply variants and completed DIV/REM values through WB and register-
file bypass, in real and ALTOPS builds. Stress retained invalid WB data
while an intervening memory request stalls and a younger instruction
uses that value as its address base. Check exact RVFI source/result and
memory fields, stable stalled requests, retirement order and unchanged
instruction timing. Run unchanged standard formal, real arithmetic tests,

title: Two-entry elastic fetch queue with validity-independent payload capture
motivation:
The champion achieves 174.44 iter/sec at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Structural divider retimings in rounds
eight and nine gained less than one percent as other paths limited
frequency. Round ten's one-entry fall-through fetch buffer reduced
cycles to 4,022,833 but reached only 72.497 MHz and 180.21 iter/sec,
a 3.31-percent gain below acceptance. This establishes useful
instruction-stall overlap, but one saved response fills immediately
during a multi-cycle backend hold. Adding a second saved response
can exploit those remaining fetch opportunities while retaining
the same two-way decode-output selection depth.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion achieves 174.44 iter/sec at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Structural divider retimings in rounds
eight and nine gained less than one percent as other paths limited
frequency. Round ten's one-entry fall-through fetch buffer reduced
cycles to 4,022,833 but reached only 72.497 MHz and 180.21 iter/sec,
a 3.31-percent gain below acceptance. This establishes useful
instruction-stall overlap, but one saved response fills immediately
during a multi-cycle backend hold. Adding a second saved response
can exploit those remaining fetch opportunities while retaining
the same two-way decode-output selection depth.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the lockstep frontend with a two-entry fall-through FIFO
implemented as fixed head and tail registers. This is one structural
change: decouple fetch progress from backend progress with two
instruction slots. Preserve the existing predictor algorithm,
arithmetic units, backend stage count and single retirement width.
Each slot contains the instruction, its PC and the predicted_taken
bit captured when that bus response was accepted. The request PC
addresses the next response, independently of the decode-head PC.

Decode sees head when head_valid, otherwise the live response.
Keep this as one two-input payload mux; do not introduce an indexed
queue read or a third tail input in the combinational decode path.
Move tail into head only across a clock edge. The valid states are
empty, head-only and head-plus-tail; tail_valid implies head_valid.
Export fetch_available = head_valid || io_imemReady to the hazard
unit in place of physical instruction ready. Both late-use detection
and prospective forwarding MUST compare the selected decode-head
source fields, rather than raw io_imemData. Payload selection must
depend only on registered occupancy, independently of flush,
redirect and decode validity. Separate payload assignments from
validity assignments to avoid combinational recovery/hazard loops.

Let consume = !stall, where stall is the frontend hold computed
using fetch_available and existing backend interlocks. Outside
reset/recovery, accept a response when io_imemReady &&
(!tail_valid || consume). Advance the request PC and its prediction
only on this fetch acceptance. The payload update cases are:
empty plus consume passes the accepted response directly to ID;
empty plus hold saves an accepted response in head; head-only plus
consume replaces head with an accepted response or becomes empty;
head-only plus hold appends an accepted response to tail; full plus
consume promotes tail to head and replaces tail if a response is
accepted; full plus hold preserves both slots and the request PC.
This permits one instruction per cycle with continuously ready
buses and consumes queued instructions while io_imemReady is low.
A response that bypasses an empty queue is not also enqueued.

Separate payload capture from response acceptance and validity.
This detail is essential to the measured candidate. Let stall be the
same frontend hold above, response={request_pc,imem_data,prediction},
and head_q/tail_q be packed 65-bit payload registers. Outside reset:
  head_load = head_valid ^ stall;
  tail_load = head_valid && (!tail_valid || !stall);
  if (head_load) head_q <= tail_valid ? tail_q : response;
  if (tail_load) tail_q <= response.
Do not qualify these wide payload enables with imemReady, fetch_accept,
redirect or flush. They intentionally capture some invalid responses;
validity alone determines whether a captured response may be consumed.
When head is empty and decode holds, it may sample an unready response
but stays invalid; when a full queue is held, both payloads retain.
On consuming a full queue, head receives the valid tail while tail
may sample an unready response and become invalid. Capturing into an
invalid tail during a head-only dequeue is also harmless.

For occupancy, reset or redirect clears both valid bits. Otherwise,
if !stall, set head_valid_next = head_valid &&
(tail_valid || fetch_accept), tail_valid_next = tail_valid &&
fetch_accept. Otherwise, if fetch_accept, set head_valid_next=1 and
tail_valid_next=old_head_valid. Otherwise retain both valid bits.
Request PC reset/recovery retains highest priority; on a normal edge
advance it only on fetch_accept. Recovery installs redirect_target
and flushes younger ID/EX validity, even if the instruction bus is
stalled. Any same-edge wrong-path payload capture remains invalid.
Reset initializes both payload registers deterministically. Compute
predictions from the actual request PC and its bus instruction;
never recompute a buffered prediction at dequeue. Retain branch
target alignment checks, JALR recovery and one training event per
advancing branch. No buffered instruction may execute, train,
access data memory or retire before reaching its normal stage.

Preserve load/multiply dependency bubbles, youngest-producer
forwarding priority, retained MEM/WB forwarding data during data
stalls, blocking divider operand capture and nine-cycle occupancy,
exact real and ALTOPS arithmetic, decoder legality, misalignment
traps and all external memory handshakes. Do not change nret=1,
RVFI ports, ordered exact-once retirement, formal depths or any
correctness gate. A full queue must remain lossless through
arbitrarily long backend holds; progress under ready buses must
retain the existing formal bound.

An isolated RTL prototype of this exact two-entry fall-through queue
and payload capture scheme completed canonical stalled CoreMark in
3,981,061 bracketed cycles, versus 4,230,003 for the champion, and
passed the canonical CRCs, UART validation, marker and bounds checks.
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 70.727,73.832,73.832 MHz,
median 73.832 MHz. Preliminary fitness is 185.45810 iter/sec, a
6.32-percent gain over 174.44, above the required 182.46424 threshold.
Option-zero resources were 5,557 LUT4s, 1,346 registers, 40 LUT-RAMs,
four BSRAMs and two DSPs. The six-percent forecast rounds this result;
reproduce it on implementation before claiming champion replacement.

Response-qualified, priority-selected payload writes in an otherwise
identical two-entry queue measured only 59.337 MHz, despite identical
CoreMark cycles. Thus merely adding capacity is insufficient: retain
the simple payload equations and separate valid-bit discipline above.
The exact refinement passed all 38 real pipeline cases and the six
multiply-focused ALTOPS pipeline cases after adapting the independent
frontend model. It also passed 2,500 randomized frontend transactions
against an independent list-based queue, including all occupancies,
full consume/refill, held-full state, response stalls, redirects and
reset of a full queue. Selftest and three random programs each passed
full RVFI cosimulation with and without both bus stalls, eight cases.
The exact final refinement passed all 53 unchanged nret=1 ALTOPS
formal checks, including register consistency, legality, ordered
retirement and liveness. Formal used the original wrapper_si.sv
and checks_si.cfg properties/depths in isolated generated staging.
Rerun every required qualification check on implementation. Real-M
formal-deep was not run; arithmetic RTL and ALTOPS formulas are
unchanged.
Main risks are synthesis/routing differences consuming the remaining
margin, incorrect invalid-payload handling, and regressions in saved
predictions or retained forwarding across longer independent fetches.

Preserve existing test coverage and update frontend scheduling
models to track the independent request stream and a two-element
reference queue. Cover all occupancies, bypass, head replacement,
tail promotion, simultaneous full dequeue/refill, instruction-bus
stalls during queued issue, data stalls, load/multiply-use bubbles,
divisions, saved predictions changing before dequeue, reset and
redirect with each occupancy. Check wrong-path store/divider
cancellation, same-rd producer priority, x0, RVFI PC/operand/order
traces and accepted-store counts. Trigger data stalls from active
requests, rather than assumptions that fetch PC equals decode PC.
Run unchanged formal and architectural cosimulation, canonical
stalled CoreMark with every CRC, UART text, memory bound and marker
check, and Gowin timing across the evaluator's placement options.

title: Register the alternate successor for direct-branch recovery
motivation:
The champion's reported worst path runs from a forwarding mask through
EX branch resolution into the fetch PC. The current recovery datapath
uses the late actual_taken result both to detect a miss and to select
its 32-bit destination. Exact direct-target prediction makes that
second dependency unnecessary: a direction miss always needs the
alternative to the prediction already accepted at fetch. Prior
counter shrinking, Gray encoding and parallel predicate experiments
did not clear the threshold. Profiling also found only 13,735 JALRs
in the measured region, limiting the upside of an indirect predictor.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Precompute and register one alternate successor address with each
fetched instruction. In if_stage, reuse the existing predicted_target
and PC+4 arithmetic and define
out.recovery_pc = predicted_taken ? (pc + 32'd4) : predicted_target.
Add a 32-bit recovery_pc to IF/ID and ID/EX. Capture it under the
existing !stall ID/EX payload enable and hold it through stalls.
Reset the bundle normally; flushing need only clear validity and
the existing prediction bit, not the wide recovery_pc payload.

In EX replace only recovery target selection with
redirect_target = in.ctrl.is_jalr ? jump_target : in.recovery_pc.
Keep the existing advancing && (actual_taken != in.predicted_taken)
redirect equation and all its reset, validity and stall qualification.
Do not change branch comparisons, branch_taken, actual_taken,
misalignment logic, branch training or actual EX/MEM pc_next.
All controls selecting recovery data are now ID/EX register outputs.
The late forwarded branch comparison controls whether to recover,
without also selecting or generating a direct recovery address.
This is one predictor-recovery architecture change, with no added
pipeline stage or misprediction cycle.

A predicted-not-taken branch that actually takes uses the registered
exact branch target. A predicted-taken branch that falls through uses
registered PC+4. Retain the 64-entry agree predictor, aligned exact
B/J prediction and unpredicted JALR. An aligned JAL is predicted
correctly. Misaligned direct transfers are never predicted taken
and retain the existing trap/linear-PC behavior. JALR continues to
select its actual forwarded, bit-zero-cleared jump_target and uses
the existing alignment suppression. recovery_pc for nontransfers
and redirect_target while redirect is false are unused; do not
substitute either for the architectural next PC reported through RVFI.

Keep recovery limited to fetch PC selection and validity. Do not put
redirect on raw instruction data, source-index paths, or recovery_pc
payload enables. Preserve recovery priority over instruction-bus
stalls, deferral during older dmem stalls and execute holds, exact-once
memory effects, forwarding, arithmetic and ALTOPS, decoder legality,
nret=1 ports, ordered retirement and unchanged bounded progress.
Keep full 32-bit target semantics; do not specialize addresses to
CoreMark or the memory bounds.

An isolated prototype of this exact registered-target change passed
all 38 pipeline tests and six multiply/ALTOPS pipeline tests after
updating only packed-bundle widths and field offsets for the added
metadata. Canonical CoreMark with both bus stalls retained exactly
4,230,003 marker-bracketed cycles, all five canonical CRCs, the required
validation text, normal completion and no out-of-bounds accesses.
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 70.253, 71.597 and 71.597 MHz.
Option zero used 5,306 LUT4s and 1,245 registers, versus the champion's
5,422 and 1,214, with unchanged RAM and DSP counts. Median fitness is
169.25993 iter/sec, approximately 2.97 percent BELOW the champion.
The limiting reported path moved to the first divider recurrence.

These measurements do not qualify this prototype as a replacement.
The negative forecast below records the measured limitation rather
than claiming that removing a recovery dependency guarantees a faster
whole core. The intended timing benefit remains the earlier recovery
address, but unchanged divider and forwarded-ALU paths can dominate.
Do not combine unrelated arithmetic, table or memory changes to rescue
this slot. Keep the champion unless the final implementation measures
strictly above 182.46424 iter/sec; at unchanged cycles this requires
median Gowin Fmax above 77.18243 MHz.

Run the unchanged formal suite and full-RVFI cosimulation on the final
implementation; the prototype's pipeline and benchmark checks do not
replace those gates. In particular prove that whenever redirect is
asserted, redirect_target equals the actual architectural successor.

assertions, adapting only packed-layout references to the new field.

forwarded and held operands, direct and indirect jumps, misaligned
targets, instruction stalls concurrent with recovery, reset and
divider completion. Reproduce canonical CoreMark and all three
vendor timing options before evaluating acceptance.

title: Predecode load versus arithmetic writeback forwarding before EX
motivation:
The champion reaches 174.44 iterations/sec at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its EX operands already use registered one-hot
forwarding masks, but the MEM/WB candidate still passes through wb_stage's
mem_to_reg mux before entering those operand muxes. This serial selection
affects branches, ALU results, memory addresses and divider operand capture.
Prior micro_opt branch rewrites (r8s0, r9s0 and r10s0) did not improve the
champion; r11s0 moved final result selection before MEM/WB and separated
address generation, but gained only 1.75 percent. Test a distinct placement
of the same forwarding decision: predecode its control in ID while keeping
both existing MEM/WB data registers and their input arithmetic unchanged.

hypothesis.motivation:

bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its EX operands already use registered one-hot
forwarding masks, but the MEM/WB candidate still passes through wb_stage's
mem_to_reg mux before entering those operand muxes. This serial selection
affects branches, ALU results, memory addresses and divider operand capture.

champion; r11s0 moved final result selection before MEM/WB and separated

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Flatten the EX operand selection by treating MEM/WB arithmetic data and
MEM/WB load data as separate, mutually exclusive forwarding candidates.
Resolve their selection at the existing ID/EX edge, alongside the existing
prospective producer-tag comparisons. This is one local mux/control
optimization; add no pipeline stage, instruction latency or interlock.

Widen each raw source mask from three to four bits: bit 0 selects the
captured register-file value, bit 1 selects EX/MEM.alu_result, bit 2 selects
MEM/WB.alu_result, and bit 3 selects MEM/WB.read_data. In forward_unit retain
the existing younger-writer priority and x0 exclusion. Compute young_hit
exactly as today; compute old_hit with the current older-writer enable and
tag match and !young_hit. Set bit 2 to old_hit && !old_mem_to_reg and bit 3
to old_hit && old_mem_to_reg; bit 0 is !(young_hit || old_hit). The new
old_mem_to_reg input MUST come from ex_mem_w.ctrl.mem_to_reg: that is the
producer about to enter MEM/WB on the edge capturing these masks. Do not
use the current mem_wb_w control, which belongs to a different instruction.

Expand the registered ALU-source masks consistently to five bits, with
bit 4 selecting PC for operand A or immediate for operand B. Decode masks
off all four register candidates for AUIPC or an immediate ALU operand,
just as the existing three register candidates are masked off today.
Update explicit widths, concatenations and reset values consistently.
Preserve the original raw operand values independently for store data,
branch comparison, division operands and RVFI.

Wire MEM/WB.alu_result and MEM/WB.read_data directly to separate EX inputs.
Implement raw operands as a masked OR of their four original data sources
using the saved one-hot masks. Implement complete ALU operands similarly,
with the fifth PC/immediate source. Never reconstruct a load-versus-ALU
mux ahead of either forwarding network and never select using live WB
mem_to_reg in EX. Keep wb_stage and its ordinary writeback mux unchanged
for the register-file write port, write-first read bypass and RVFI rd data.
Preserve MEM/WB's existing input mux for multiply reconstruction: a
completed multiply is an arithmetic WB candidate in real and ALTOPS builds.

Keep the original producer qualification, including trap suppression,
the younger multiply exclusion, next_reg_write behavior and load/multiply
dependency bubble. A just-completed division remains eligible as the
younger EX/MEM producer. Do not qualify held MEM/WB forwarding data with
architectural WB valid or w_en. During dmem backpressure ID/EX masks and
both MEM/WB data fields retain their values under the existing enables;
clearing retirement valid must not change which saved operand is used.
The division request still captures fully forwarded operands at launch.
Preserve all reset/flush/hold priorities, traps, bus requests, predictor
behavior, nret=1 ports and exact RVFI retirement ordering.

The expected benefit is removal of one serial result-type selection from
the WB-to-EX operand cone without adding a mux before either MEM/WB data
register, unlike r11s0. It also removes live mem_to_reg fanout from these
EX data paths. The costs are wider saved masks, extra data wiring and
four/five-way masked-OR fan-in. Gowin may refactor the muxes or unrelated
divider recurrence paths may limit timing, so the eight-percent fitness
forecast has low confidence and is not a measured result. This proposal
deliberately retains the existing divider arithmetic and prediction policy.

Validate the mask invariant against the old forwarding formula and test
arithmetic/load/multiply/divide producers, both consumer operands, x0,
same-rd younger priority, immediate ALU operations and AUIPC. Specifically
alternate load and arithmetic producers across EX/MEM and MEM/WB so a
one-stage error in the sampled mem_to_reg is detected. Exercise a WB
producer followed by an unrelated stalled memory instruction and a held
dependent branch/store/ALU consumer; check retained data after WB valid
clears. Include illegal instructions and misaligned memory/jump traps.
Retain all current assertions and cycle checks, standard ALTOPS formal,
real arithmetic unit tests and RVFI cosimulation with both buses stalled.
Canonical CoreMark should remain at 4,230,003 marker-bracketed cycles for
the same stall sequence, with every CRC/UART/bounds check intact. Score
all three Gowin placement options; acceptance requires fitness strictly
above 182.46424 iterations/sec, approximately 77.183 MHz at those cycles.

title: Replace ID/EX with a WB-snooping three-entry in-order instruction queue
motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 iter/sec at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003 CoreMark
cycles. Structural attempts r10s1 and r11s1 demonstrated that fetching

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the single ID/EX register with a three-entry, strictly in-order
instruction queue: one fixed head that is the EX instruction, and two
waiting entries. Fetch, decode and register-file reads operate on the
live instruction-bus response before enqueue. EX always reads the fixed
head register. This is one structural change to the decode/execute
boundary, with no extra pipeline stage, wider issue, cache or predictor
change. Two waiting slots provide the buffering capacity that r11s1
demonstrated was useful, without its raw-instruction selection mux in
front of decode, immediate generation and register-file reads.

Each entry holds the existing decoded instruction metadata, PC, immediate,
destination and source addresses, original instruction, saved prediction,
and two captured register operand values. These values represent the
latest committed register state, not speculative results from older
queued instructions. While an entry waits, snoop every actual WB write:
when wb_w_en && wb_w_addr!=0 matches either saved source address, update
that source value from wb_w_data. All retiring writers are older than
every queued instruction because execution and retirement remain ordered.
This makes WB snooping sufficient without a rename map, producer tokens,
reservation stations or out-of-order execution. Suppressed writes from
illegal or misaligned instructions must never update saved operands.

Preserve the existing WB write-first behavior for incoming operands.
On a queue shift, apply the same-edge WB update to the payload being
promoted, rather than relying on a nonblocking assignment to its old
slot; otherwise the promoted instruction can miss the last older write.
Apply snoops during backend and instruction-bus stalls as well as normal
advancement. x0 stays zero. The head's committed operand snapshots may
update while held, but its instruction/control/PC stay stable. Once a
divider request launches, continue using its already captured operands
and metadata, independently of later queue operand snoops.

Keep EX's one-hot register/EX-MEM/MEM-WB operand selection, including
youngest-writer priority and PC/immediate selection. Forward only from
older executed producers in EX/MEM and MEM/WB. Compute the head's source
masks prospectively across the queue-advance edge, from the source tags
of the instruction that will occupy the head and the producer stages
that will exist after that edge. Register the masks before EX arithmetic;
do not add a source-index comparator followed by a mux to the EX critical
path. Unlike the current held ID/EX masks, refresh the masks when older
stages advance while the queue head waits. Preserve retained MEM/WB
data on genuine dmem holds, and distinguish architectural WB write enable
from eligibility of retained forwarding data. An older invalid pipeline
bubble must not override the saved committed operand value.

A queued consumer can become head behind an immediately preceding load
or multiply, but cannot issue until the required result is available.
Detect this from the head's source tags and the older late producer in
EX/MEM, not from raw io_imemData. Inject an inert EX/MEM bubble while the
producer advances into MEM/WB, then issue using the registered WB source
mask. Preserve the existing one-cycle dependency cost and the priority
of older memory backpressure. Conservative raw-source comparisons may
be retained; source-use filtering is not part of this hypothesis. Never
forward an effective address or multiply partial product as register
data. Gate divider launch, branch resolution, training, memory effects
and EX/MEM advancement with actual head issue and operand availability.

Fetch acceptance is independent of head issue: accept a ready response
whenever the queue has free space or the head leaves on the same edge.
Let dequeue mean that this head really transfers to EX/MEM, including a
completed divider transfer; starting a division does not dequeue it.
Dmem backpressure, a pending late operand, and an active divider retain
the head, while available tail space can still capture new instructions.
Full simultaneous dequeue/enqueue sustains one instruction per cycle.
If empty, an accepted response becomes the registered head on that edge,
exactly where the baseline would have captured ID/EX. Do not add a
separate registered IF/ID stage or combinationally execute a live response.

Use fixed head and waiting-slot registers, shift younger entries only
across a clock edge, and keep EX's head payload free of an output mux.
Separate wide payload capture/shift and operand-snoop enables from
occupancy and kill logic. It is safe to sample invalid incoming payloads,
but never overwrite a valid held payload or mark an unaccepted response
valid. Track occupancy explicitly and exercise all four occupancies.
The request PC advances only for an accepted bus response. Compute the
existing exact direct-target/agree prediction using that request PC and
response, and store predicted_taken at enqueue. Do not recompute saved
predictions as entries advance through the queue.

On EX recovery, the resolving head still advances exactly once; kill
every younger queued instruction and any same-edge wrong-path response,
install redirect_target in the request PC, and admit no younger side
effects. Recovery retains priority over an instruction-bus stall. Reset
empties the queue, cancels division and initializes state deterministically.
Preserve the decoder's default-illegal validation, all alignment traps,
existing arithmetic and ALTOPS formulas, nine-cycle division scheduling,
nret=1 ports, memory handshakes and monotonic exact-once channel-0 RVFI.
Keep the unchanged liveness bound; no formal-depth or wrapper changes.

This final instruction-queue design is an unmeasured hypothesis. It must
not inherit timing or correctness claims from other queue placements.
During hypothesis exploration, an isolated two-entry predecoded fetch
buffer preserved 3,981,061 cycles and passed eight architectural cosims,
5,000 independent FIFO transactions and all 53 unchanged formal checks,
but reached only 68.831 MHz. Rotating raw and decoded fetch queues also
missed the timing target. A separate registered two-entry fetch queue
took 4,068,383 cycles at 72.513 MHz and failed liveness despite passing
the CoreMark CRCs and architectural cosims. A four-entry registered fetch
queue took 4,030,415 cycles at 70.673 MHz. These results motivate replacing
ID/EX rather than adding storage ahead of it. None is the proposed design.

The six-percent forecast assumes recovering approximately the prior
two-slot buffering cycle benefit while keeping frequency near the
champion's 73.790 MHz. At 3,981,061 cycles the acceptance threshold needs
more than 72.640127 MHz. Principal risks are WB-snoop fanout and register
input muxing, incorrect prospective masks during partial advancement,
and unintended extra load-use or divider cycles. Measure actual cycles
and median Gowin Fmax; reject this hypothesis if the product does not
exceed 182.46424 iter/sec. Do not count RVFI-only optimizations as gains.

Validate the queue and snooping against an independent list-based model,
then run the unchanged complete formal suite, full RVFI cosimulation,
existing exact M-extension tests and canonical stalled CoreMark with
all five CRCs, UART validation, bounds and timing-marker checks. Explicitly
exercise the unchanged ready-bus retirement bound around branch recovery,
late-result dependencies and division. Update obsolete microarchitectural
test snapshots while retaining architectural and progress assertions.

title: Register both predictor feedback sinks without adding recovery latency
motivation:
The current critical path traverses forwarded EX branch resolution into
the fetch PC. The r8s2 split-PC experiment preserved CoreMark cycles but
moved the limiting path to agree-counter training and lost frequency.
The r5s2 training register alone also failed while other paths dominated.
These results identify two competing endpoints of the same late branch
feedback. Registering both feedback sinks together is a focused predictor
timing hypothesis: remove the remaining training bottleneck while keeping
the recovery destination separate from normal prediction arithmetic.
A timing-only ablation on the current champion with delayed training but
the original single PC register measured 72.353 MHz median, confirming
that the joint design's 74.396 MHz result depends on both feedback changes.
Better direction accuracy alone has little headroom given the recorded
approximately 46,000 misses in a 4.23-million-cycle canonical run.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Introduce one common register boundary for EX-to-frontend feedback in
if_stage. Keep the existing 64-entry, two-bit, locally updated agree
predictor, PC[7:2] indexing, exact aligned B/J targets and unpredicted JALR.
This is one predictor feedback architecture change, covering both late
resolution sinks rather than retiming the PC and leaving table training
on its original EX-to-counter path. No execution stage or miss bubble
is added, and no arithmetic or memory architecture changes are proposed.

Replace the single PC register with predicted_pc_q, recovery_pc_q and
recovery_active_q. The selected architectural fetch PC is
recovery_active_q ? recovery_pc_q : predicted_pc_q; use it everywhere
the current fetch PC is used, including immediate arithmetic and lookup.
Reset both banks to RESET_PC and the selector to zero. On every !stall
edge capture the existing predicted next_pc in predicted_pc_q. Capture
redirect_target in recovery_pc_q when !recovery_active_q OR redirect.
Set recovery_active_q on redirect; otherwise clear it on !stall and
hold it during stalls. Reset has highest priority. A new redirect must
override an active recovery bank and any instruction-bus stall.
Keep these distinct bank assignments rather than reconstructing the
original three-way next-PC mux in front of either bank.

An EX miss therefore captures and selects its recovery address on the
original recovery edge. A stalled target fetch retains the active bank;
accepting that fetch writes its predicted successor into the other bank
and switches back. There is no delayed redirect to the pipeline: retain
the existing same-cycle EX redirect and validity-only IF/ID squashes.
Prove that the selected PC obeys exactly the existing reset, redirect,
accept and hold recurrence. Inactive-bank writes have no architectural
effect. Do not extend the divider retirement gap or formal liveness bound.

At this same frontend feedback boundary register each qualified training
event as an eight-bit one-hot bank enable, a three-bit row and an agreement
bit. On every non-reset edge set bank_q to train_valid ?
(8'b1 << train_index[5:3]) : 8'b0. Capture row_q=train_index[2:0] and
agree_q=train_agree when train_valid; reset all event fields to zero.
Counter entry e consumes the previous cycle's event when bank_q[e/8]
and row_q==e%8, using the original binary saturating transition on its
current local two-bit state. Keep counter reset at weak agreement 2'b10.
No second indexed training read or pending-update bypass is introduced.

Accept and consume one event each cycle, including consecutive aliases.
Clear bank validity when no new event arrives so a hold never replays
training. A previously accepted event applies even during current imem
or dmem stalls, divider work or a younger redirect; reset cancels it.
Keep EX train_valid qualification unchanged. Delayed training may alter
nearby predictions, so carry the actual accepted predicted_taken bit
through existing metadata and let EX recover every mismatch normally.
The PC-bank selector and training-valid bits are different state: a held
recovery PC must not hold or replay a training event.

Preserve raw instruction/source-index paths, valid-only squashes, all
payload holds, forwarding, bus handshakes, alignment traps, illegal
decoding, RV32M and ALTOPS behavior, nret=1 ports and RVFI order. Use
full-width PCs without program-specific targets or initialization.

Expected benefit is a shorter EX feedback cone at both competing sinks
with roughly 45 additional state bits. The risk is that the output PC
mux or unchanged divider/ALU becomes limiting; the prior individual
experiments are evidence for this risk. An isolated prototype of this
exact joint design measured 72.382, 74.396 and 74.396 MHz across Gowin
placement options 0/1/2, for a 74.396 MHz median. Canonical CoreMark with
both bus stalls retained 4,230,003 bracketed cycles and passed all five
CRCs, UART validation, bounds, markers and completion checks. Option-zero
resources were 5,418 LUT4s and 1,259 registers, with unchanged 40 LUT RAMs,
four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Fitness is approximately 175.877 iter/sec, only
0.82 percent above 174.44: this does not qualify as a replacement.
The reported worst path moved to forwarded load data through the ALU
into data memory. The one-percent forecast records this measured gain
rather than claiming an unobserved improvement above the threshold.
Reproduce canonical bracketed cycles and median vendor Fmax together.
Acceptance requires fitness
strictly above 182.46424 iter/sec; at 4,230,003 cycles this requires
more than 77.18243 MHz. Keep the champion unless that margin is measured.

Validate the selected-PC recurrence and an independent one-event-delayed
training oracle, including reset, consecutive same-index events, lookup
concurrent with update, both direction misses, JALR, misalignment,
instruction stalls concurrent with recovery, a held recovery bank and
older dmem/divider holds. Preserve architectural and exact-once checks;
update prediction-policy timing expectations only where delayed training
actually changes the predicted direction. The isolated prototype passed
all 38 pipeline cases and six ALTOPS multiply pipeline cases after adapting
the independent event oracle. Preserve the lookup/update crossing assertion
with a directed cold forward-taken branch to an alias at PC+256, so lookup
coincides with the delayed weak-agree to weak-disagree write. Selftest and
all three random programs passed full RVFI comparison both with and without
stalls, eight cases total. All 53 unchanged single-retirement ALTOPS formal
checks also passed, including register consistency, PC continuity, unique
retirement, legality and liveness. These ran in isolated staging with the
original wrapper, properties and depths. Real-arithmetic formal-deep was
not run; arithmetic is unchanged. Reproduce these formal and full-RVFI
cosim gates and canonical CoreMark CRC, UART, bounds and marker validation
on the final implementation before evaluating all three vendor options.

title: Prepare and distribute divider operands to pairs of recurrence phases
motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 iterations/second at 73.790 MHz and
4,230,003 bracketed CoreMark cycles. The r6s1 improvement gave each
quotient/remainder phase dedicated state, but all phases still read
global D and 3D registers. The r9s0 and r10s0 micro_opt trials exposed
divisor-to-remainder timing paths, and r9s1 showed that preparing the
first narrow 3D alone merely moved the limit to EX arithmetic. Test
coordinated preparation and distribution of these same divider operands,
with a small bank shared by each pair of later recurrence phases.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Localize the existing divider's D and 3D operands in groups of recurrence
phases, and prepare phase zero's narrow 3D during operand capture. This
is one micro_opt hypothesis about registered divisor-operand preparation
and fanout. Keep the existing radix-4 equations, pipeline boundaries,
nine-cycle DIV/REM occupancy and all other CPU logic unchanged.

Retain the existing phase numbering p=0..6, with consumed prefix lengths
C=2,8,12,16,20,24,28. Define a static bank selector
BANK = p==0 ? 0 : 1 + 2*((p-1)/2).
Thus phase zero uses D bank 0; phases 1/2 share bank 1; phases 3/4
share bank 3; phases 5/6 share bank 5. Implement four 32-bit D banks
at indices 0,1,3,5 and three 34-bit 3D banks at indices 1,3,5.
Sparse constant-index arrays are sufficient; unused elements must never
be read by execution. No dynamic bank mux or scoreboard is introduced.

On accepted launch, capture divisor_magnitude in D bank 0. Also capture
launch_triple_q = {2'b0,divisor_magnitude[7:0]} +
                  {1'b0,divisor_magnitude[7:0],1'b0}
as an explicitly unsigned ten-bit value. Phase zero has P=8 and W=10;
its existing large_d bypass discards truncated divisor multiples when
any divisor bit above bit 7 is set. Therefore this is the exact required
3D for that phase. Replace only its combinational d1+d2 with this saved
value. Keep the original two-bit launch recurrence and magnitude/sign
logic, so no extra launch cycle or ALTOPS shortcut is added.

On phase zero's original enabled edge, copy D bank 0 to bank 1 and
capture full 34-bit 3D from bank 0 into triple bank 1. This is the
existing full-3D preparation slot, in parallel with the first recurrence.
On phase two's enabled edge, copy D/3D bank 1 into bank 3. On phase
four's enabled edge, copy bank 3 into bank 5. Each transfer uses exactly
active_q && !complete_q && iteration_q==p, alongside the original
quotient/remainder successor write. A group receives its divisor before
its first consuming phase and retains it through its second phase.
Do not write every bank simultaneously at launch: their distinct enabled
updates prevent trivial synthesis merging and limit launch fanout.

Use divisor_bank[BANK] for the phase's large_d guard and d1 low slice;
keep d2 as a shift. For p>0 use triple_bank[BANK][W-1:0] for d3; for
p=0 use launch_triple_q. Preserve all existing C/N/P/W constants, all
32 D bits and 34 3D bits, widened parallel trial subtractions and borrow
conventions, quotient digits, one-hot remainder selection and the
large-divisor bypass. Reset every implemented bank and launch_triple_q
to zero. Keep reset's priority, ignored starts while busy and the
accepted-start qualification exactly unchanged.

Preserve final sign correction, division by zero, INT_MIN/-1, result
retention and start/busy/done/accept behavior. Bank enables must prevent
updates during held completion. Keep the real and ALTOPS schedule
identical; the ALTOPS arithmetic branch itself remains unchanged. Retain
observation-only divisor_q and triple_divisor_q aliases of banks 0 and 1
for the existing independent arithmetic checks. Do not use a dynamically
selected observation alias in any execution calculation.

The timing rationale is to remove phase zero's serial 3D addition and
reduce each later divisor register's arithmetic fanout from six phases
to two. Four D banks, three full 3D banks and a ten-bit launch value add
174 theoretical state bits before pruning. This avoids the larger
placement cost of one complete divisor copy per individual phase.
Forwarded ALU/address logic and other divider paths can still limit Fmax.

An isolated prototype of this exact paired-phase implementation measured
Gowin options 0/1/2 at 68.717, 73.527 and 73.527 MHz, for a 73.527 MHz
median. Option zero used 5,415 LUT4s and 1,384 registers, with unchanged
40 LUT RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Its worst path was retained WB
load selection through EX arithmetic into data memory. Canonical CoreMark retained
4,230,003 cycles, yielding 173.8226 iterations/second, roughly
0.35 percent below 174.44. This is not an accepted improvement; the
integer zero-percent forecast reflects a near-neutral measured result,
not an unobserved gain above the acceptance threshold. Fully local
prepared banks measured 72.457 MHz, and one shared later bank measured
70.328 MHz, supporting the paired grouping within this one hypothesis.

The prototype passed the unchanged pipeline runner, ALTOPS multiply
pipeline runner and both real/ALTOPS divider runners, four pytest cases
covering the existing internal cocotb suites. Preserve every assertion
and exact-cycle check. Extend the independent prefix-division oracle to
check the local bank when each phase consumes it, using the original
captured magnitude rather than another DUT bank as the reference.
Cover changing divisors across consecutive requests, all signedness
combinations, high-bit and large_d boundary divisors, D=0, D=1,
INT_MIN/-1, reset during every phase, rejected busy starts and held
completion. Check launch/training dependencies and forwarded operands
under both memory-bus stalls with exact RVFI retirement and side effects.

Full RVFI cosimulation passed selftest and all three random programs,
each with and without both bus stalls, eight cases total. Canonical
CoreMark passed all five CRCs, the required UART validation text, memory
bounds, completion and timing-marker checks at exactly 4,230,003 bracketed
cycles. Full-core formal and non-ALTOPS formal-deep were not run for this
prototype and remain implementation gates. ALTOPS formal does not prove
the real bank routing; preserve the real-arithmetic tests.
Preserve nret=1 IO, illegal-default decoding, alignment traps, forwarding,
progress and exact-once retirement. Keep all CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks.
Expected CoreMark cycles remain 4,230,003 for the same stall sequence.
Acceptance still requires fitness strictly above 182.46424 iter/sec,
about 77.183 MHz at that cycle count. Retain the champion unless the
required greater-than-4.6-percent margin is actually measured.

title: Move elastic frontend selection after decode and register-file reads
motivation:
The champion scores 174.44 iter/sec at 73.790 MHz and 4,230,003
CoreMark cycles. Structural r10s1 and r11s1 demonstrated useful fetch
decoupling, but their instruction-head selection reduced frequency.
R11s1 needed 3,981,061 cycles at 71.714 MHz, yielding only 180.14
iter/sec. R12s1 moved buffering into ID/EX and snooped WB into queued
operands, but reached only 70.141 MHz. Preserve the measured two-slot

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Build one elastic frontend with two fetch-buffer slots, predecoded
instruction payloads and independent register-file read paths for
the live response and saved head. Keep the existing ID/EX, EX/MEM and
MEM/WB boundaries. This is one structural change to the placement of
frontend selection: choose between already-decoded, already-read
instruction sources immediately before ID/EX capture. Preserve the
champion's backend arithmetic, predictor algorithm and issue width.

Decode each live instruction-bus response before the queue. Its payload
contains PC, raw instruction, validated ctrl_t, immediate and the saved
predicted_taken bit. Feed the same decoded response to the empty-queue
bypass and to the queue's capture inputs. Buffer controls and immediates
along with the instruction, so the selected queue output never needs
another decoder or immediate generator. Use the existing decoder and
imm_gen; retain default-illegal behavior and every encoding check.

Supply independent asynchronous register reads for live instruction
source addresses and buffered-head source addresses. A straightforward
portable implementation is two reg_file instances receiving identical
clock, reset and actual WB writes; each instance provides two read
ports. Both copies must preserve x0 and same-cycle write-first bypass.
Select live versus saved-head register values only AFTER the reads,
using registered head occupancy. The queue stores source addresses,
not operand values. A held head therefore observes current architectural
registers on every cycle, including WB while the backend is held.
No snoop-update ports, operand version tags or new scoreboard are needed.
Allow synthesis to share storage if it preserves all four read functions.

Keep fixed head and tail slots. Decode uses saved head when valid,
otherwise the live response. Set fetch_available=head_valid||imemReady
and feed this logical availability to the existing hazard controller.
Source comparisons and prospective forwarding refer to the selected
instruction, never the next physical bus response. Preserve youngest
writer priority, the existing registered one-hot EX operand masks and
the load/multiply-use bubble. Payload selection must depend only on
occupancy, not redirect, flush or fetch validity.

Outside reset/recovery, let consume=!stall, using the frontend hold
computed with logical fetch availability and existing backend hazards.
Accept a bus response when imemReady && (!tail_valid || consume).
Advance the request PC only on acceptance, predicting from that request
PC and its actual bus instruction. Empty consume bypasses directly into
ID/EX; empty hold saves the response in head. Head-only consume replaces
head with an accepted response or empties the queue; head-only hold
appends to tail. Full consume promotes tail and optionally refills tail;
full hold preserves both entries. Sustain one instruction per cycle
with ready buses, including simultaneous full consume/refill.

Separate wide payload writes from validity. With response denoting the
live predecoded payload, use head_load=head_valid ^ stall and
tail_load=head_valid && (!tail_valid || !stall). On head_load, capture
tail_valid ? tail_payload : response; on tail_load capture response.
Do not qualify these payload enables with imemReady, redirect or flush.
Sampling an unready or wrong-path response into an invalid slot is safe;
a valid held slot must never be overwritten. For normal validity updates,
if !stall set head_valid_next=head_valid&&(tail_valid||fetch_accept)
and tail_valid_next=tail_valid&&fetch_accept. Otherwise, on acceptance,
set head_valid_next=1 and tail_valid_next=old_head_valid; otherwise hold.
Tail validity always implies head validity.

Reset empties the queue and initializes its payload deterministically.
Recovery overrides acceptance, clears both valid bits and younger
ID/EX validity, and installs redirect_target even during an instruction
bus stall. A same-edge speculative payload write remains invalid.
Save each accepted prediction; never recompute it on dequeue. Leave
exact direct targets, agree counters, training and JALR behavior intact.
Keep decode payload and source-index assignments separate from validity
assignments to avoid a combinational recovery/hazard feedback loop.

The isolated prototype preserves the expected 3,981,061 bracketed
CoreMark cycles, all canonical CRCs, validation text and memory bounds.
Selftest and three random programs pass full RVFI cosimulation both
with and without instruction/data stalls, eight passing trace cases.
The proposed prototype measured placement options 0/1/2 at
69.791/70.084/70.084 MHz, median 70.084 MHz, using 5,951 LUT4s,
1,420 registers and 80 LUT RAMs. Calculated fitness is 176.04352 iter/sec,
only 0.9192 percent above 174.44. This DOES NOT clear the required
182.46424 iter/sec acceptance threshold. At 3,981,061 cycles, acceptance
requires median Fmax above 72.640127 MHz. The one-percent forecast
reflects the measured small gain, not a claim of a qualifying replacement.
A separate variant moving forwarding/hazard tag comparisons before
selection regressed to 62.349 MHz and is explicitly not proposed.
Repeat the implementation and all required gates before judging the
candidate; the acceptance margin must not be relaxed.

Main risks are extra register-file write fanout, replication area,
control/operand muxing before ID/EX, and the unchanged backend becoming
timing-limiting. Measure the median over all vendor placement options;
do not count pruned RVFI logic or a single favorable option as a gain.
Keep nret=1 ports, exact-once channel-0 RVFI order, all traps, original
real and ALTOPS arithmetic, nine-cycle division scheduling, stable
blocked memory requests and the unchanged formal liveness bound.

Validate the queue against an independent FIFO and architectural
register model, stressing writes while a head waits, same-edge WB and
dequeue, youngest producer overrides, x0, every occupancy transition,
both bus stalls, redirects at full occupancy, and reset. Run unchanged
formal, exact M-extension tests and canonical stalled CoreMark. Update
only obsolete frontend scheduling snapshots; preserve architectural,
arithmetic, progress and exact-once assertions.

All 53 unchanged nret=1 ALTOPS formal checks passed in isolated staging.
Real-M formal-deep was not run; arithmetic RTL is unchanged.

title: Split agree-predictor direction flops from RAM-backed confidence
motivation:
The 64-entry agree predictor's capacity and two-bit hysteresis already
give good CoreMark behavior. Shrinking its table caused aliases, and
r7s2's one-bit RAM lost hysteresis. Moving both bits into native RAM in
an isolated current-core prototype retained 4,230,003 bracketed cycles
but reduced median Gowin Fmax to 65.789 MHz; protecting the fetch lookup
matters. Instead separate the bit that fetch needs from confidence,
which only training needs. This preserves the existing one-bit flop
lookup while removing half the per-entry flop state and local counter
arithmetic. It is one predictor storage/update architecture change.
